name: Reference exists and its metadata match the record
definition: A reference cannot be found in Crossref/OpenAlex (possibly fabricated), its DOI is unregistered or points to a different work, or its title, authors, year or venue materially disagree with the registry record.
divergence: jaanch does this by model-orchestrated web lookup (Crossref query.bibliographic + OpenAlex) starting from map.json references, from rendered paper text, with a 'materially wrong' judgment and no thresholds; write-empirical-paper has deterministic check_bibliography.py over the .bib (title SequenceMatcher >= 0.75 or containment, year slack 1, first-author surname warn-only, DOI 404 = error, no-match search = warn) plus a manual field list that adds version, URL and access path. jaanch also searches OpenAlex (covers books/DataCite better); the wep script is Crossref-only, so DataCite DOIs 404 and books show as 'no match'. audit-analysis has no existence/metadata check at all.
validation: metacheck ref_accuracy: ~8% false-flag rate at default (3% conservative), catches 96-100% of corrupted journal/year (validated mostly on Psychological Science papers; DOI references only). Reviewer3 self-reports 98.5% accuracy separating real vs fabricated citations (methodology not seen). PaperAudit-Bench: RF is one injected-error category; overall best model 55.8% F1 Detection@1 (not per-category). No measured accuracy for jaanch or write-empirical-paper versions.
reason: Fabricated or wrong reference breaks the citation record; verified against Crossref/OpenAlex.

name: Reference carries a DOI or a suggested one
definition: A journal/proceedings entry lacks a DOI (warn), or lacks both DOI and URL under --require-doi (error); a Crossref title+first-author search may suggest the missing DOI.
divergence: Direct conflict: jaanch_check_references says 'A missing DOI is not a problem'; write-empirical-paper's check_bibliography.py warns on every DOI-less entry (error with --require-doi). Defensible split by role (reviewing someone else's paper vs preparing one's own bib), but the consolidator must pick per mode.
reason: Required DOI field missing from bibliography entry.

name: Cited work not retracted, corrected or under concern
definition: A cited work has been retracted, corrected or given an expression of concern, especially when cited as support.
divergence: jaanch runs the external `retract` tool if installed, else Crossref update-to relation, per review, and rates a retracted supporting cite at least major. write-empirical-paper only mentions a monthly GitHub Action carried over (implementation not in the skill). metacheck matches DOIs against the Retraction Watch database and also flags corrections and expressions of concern; Crossref update-to coverage of Retraction Watch is now merged but jaanch's fallback does not explicitly cover expressions of concern. audit-analysis: none.
reason: Retracted support undermines cited evidence; needs retraction database.

name: Citation supports the claim it is cited for
definition: A load-bearing citation does not say what the paper attributes to it, says the opposite, holds only under omitted conditions, or differs in direction, population or magnitude.
divergence: jaanch caps at 25 most load-bearing citations, reads abstract/text, and 'absence of access is not a finding'. audit-analysis states the stricter three-way bar (direction, population, magnitude) but with no cap, no lookup procedure and no access rule. jaanch's 'only under conditions the paper leaves out' and audit-analysis's 'population' overlap but magnitude is only in audit-analysis. write-empirical-paper has no fidelity check (only metadata).
validation: None measured for any tool. Black Spatula ~10% wrong-error rate is secondary press only (unverified).
reason: Citation must say what is claimed; requires reading the cited work.

name: In-text citations and reference list match
definition: An in-text citation has no reference entry (undefined key), or a reference entry is never cited when the style requires.
divergence: write-empirical-paper reads LaTeX/BibTeX logs (no dedicated script; method model); metacheck parses PDFs via GROBID. jaanch does not check this.
validation: metacheck module says under development with high false positives from GROBID parsing.
reason: In-text keys and reference list disagree.

name: BibTeX parses and keys are unique
definition: A .bib block cannot be parsed, or a citation key appears in more than one entry.
divergence: Only write-empirical-paper (check_bibliography.py, bibtexparser).
reason: Bibliography must parse with unique keys; fixed format rule.

name: Entry has title, year, author and venue
definition: An entry lacks a title, a year/date, both author and editor (error), or the venue field its type requires (warn).
divergence: Only write-empirical-paper.
reason: Required bibliographic fields missing.

name: Cite the official dataset, documentation or software
definition: A dataset, document or software package is cited through a secondary or unofficial source rather than its official record.
reason: Source must be the official record; needs outside lookup.

name: Each data source cited as data and accessible
definition: A data source is not itself cited (only a paper about it is), its DOI/URL does not work, or its access conditions are not described.
divergence: No tool of ours requires a data citation distinct from a paper citation; write-empirical-paper official_source_cited is the nearest (prefers the official record) but does not test access conditions or link resolution.
reason: Data source must be cited and reachable; requires checking links.

name: Benchmark source cited down to table and assumptions
definition: A benchmark is used without citing the exact source table, geography, age bands and assumptions used to construct it.
reason: Benchmark provenance (table, geography, assumptions) required but missing.

name: Cited work has post-publication PubPeer comments
definition: A cited DOI has PubPeer comments (excluding statcheck bot) the author may need to account for.
reason: Post-publication critique of cited work found on PubPeer.

name: Replications of a cited original are also cited
definition: A cited original study has replication/reproduction studies in FLoRA that the paper does not cite.
reason: Citing an original without its replications misstates the evidence; FLoRA lookup.

name: Reference is a known frequently miscited work
definition: A reference matches a database of commonly miscited works.
validation: Proof of concept; database not yet populated.
reason: Matched against a database of commonly miscited works.

name: Comment quote is verbatim in the paper
definition: A review comment's quoted span does not occur in the paper text (exactly or above a fuzzy threshold), so the comment is dropped.
divergence: Only jaanch among ours anchors quotes (NFKC, de-hyphenate, casefold, rapidfuzz partial_ratio >= 90, one threshold for all text). coarse uses a stricter threshold for math. audit-analysis, assess-empirical-claims and write-referee-report require 'quote or locate the exact claim' in prose but have no mechanical anchor. jaanch drops unanchored candidates silently at merge (listed, not repaired), which can discard correct findings with misquoted spans.
validation: No measured FP/FN for the 90 threshold (asserted in a code comment only). Anchoring proves the quote exists, not that the finding is right.
reason: Review quote compared to paper text; about the review.

name: Review's statements about the paper are true of it
definition: A comment asserts the paper omits or claims something that the paper's own text (earlier definition, footnote, appendix, robustness table, caveat, stated contribution) contradicts.
divergence: jaanch searches for the paper's existing answer per candidate inside the skeptic batch (up to 5 per agent); assess-empirical-claims applies it only to 'they ignored a rival explanation' charges; corrigendum treats the article's stated definitions as evidence that can override an audit. None of ours has a separate claim-level judge like King & Worthington.
validation: King & Worthington judge: caught 258/258 planted false sentences with 0/258 false alarms; flagged 5.5% of AI vs 15.9% of human review claims as incorrect. jaanch skeptics: 135/136 candidates confirmed, 0 refuted in the initial wave (strategies.md:131), flagged as a calibration problem, i.e. no evidence the rebuttal search removes anything.
reason: Review statements checked against the paper's own text.

name: Each candidate finding independently re-derived before acceptance
definition: A finding is accepted on the proposer's reasoning without an independent recomputation, re-derivation, rerun or lookup by a second pass that is allowed to refute it.
divergence: jaanch: separate skeptic agents, batches of 5, read-only on paper text, verdict refuted/confirmed/plausible, refute only on evidence (uncertainty -> plausible, kept). audit-analysis: the same auditor runs an adversarial pass then a validation pass, and validation must re-derive from raw/analytical data and run the distinguishing estimator (rerun, not text); only findings surviving both are kept, so 'plausible' has no home except 'speculative'. functional-form-sensitivity requires a second route with the user's own code, not the run's. assess-empirical-claims and write-referee-report apply it only to findings imported from other audits/reviewers.
validation: jaanch: 135/136 confirmed, 0 refuted (initial wave) -> skeptic not discriminating. audit-analysis bug-taxonomy lists three delegated findings that did NOT survive re-derivation (anecdotal, no rate). No measured rate for others.
reason: Second pass re-derives reviewer findings; checks the review.

name: Attack each headline result before reporting
definition: A headline result is passed without trying unit arithmetic, alternative denominators, negative controls, influence checks, external benchmarks and the strongest rival explanation.
divergence: Only audit-analysis has an explicit attack-the-headline pass. jaanch generates candidates through finders (reasoning/consistency/completeness) but has no pass whose job is to break the main result; assess-empirical-claims prioritizes consequential checks but does not mandate the attack list.
reason: Reviewer step attacking headline results by recomputation.

name: Criticism names the violated comparison and rules out conventions
definition: A criticism rests on a surprising number, an imprecise statement of what the authors compare, an estimator-convention mismatch, or an unvalidated external comparator rather than a named violated assumption, comparison or range.
divergence: audit-analysis requires comparators from primary sources matched on population/period/measurement/units; assess-empirical-claims requires matching estimator conventions before declaring a published number wrong; jaanch-experimental proposed writing the authors' claimed comparison first (not in production prompts).
validation: jaanch-experimental dev case 02 motivated it; key validity uncertain; not measured.
reason: Quality standard for a reviewer's criticism.

name: Counterexample satisfies the paper's assumptions and quantifiers
definition: A reviewer's counterexample violates a stated assumption or domain, mismatches the theorem's quantifiers, or does not say which implication (identity, proof step, theorem, interpretation) it defeats.
divergence: Experimental only; no production tool of ours checks the reviewer's witness. The round2 addendum (witness+conclusion calibration) failed its gate.
validation: Round2: reduced argument narrowing 1 -> 0 but detected 1 of 2 targets vs 2 of 2 baseline; gate failed. Others untested.
reason: Validity of the reviewer's counterexample.

name: Number-changing finding shows old and new value
definition: A numerical concern does not give both the published and corrected number with a runnable reproduction (or the mechanism, scope and replacement result), and is not labeled speculative.
divergence: audit-analysis and corrigendum require a rerun-backed corrected value; jaanch requires only that a comment be 'computed where computable' from the text (no rerun, no corrected value field). A jaanch 'confirmed' comment can therefore be what audit-analysis would label speculative.
reason: Reviewer finding must carry old and new values.

name: Comment names passage, problem, evidence and consequence
definition: A comment is generic advice, praise or summary, or lacks a manuscript location, what is wrong and how it is known, its consequence, or a feasible remedy.
divergence: jaanch demands passage + what + how known (enforced partly via the quote anchor); write-referee-report adds consequence and feasible remedy for major issues. jaanch has a fix_effort field but no remedy requirement.
reason: Comment must name passage, problem, evidence, consequence.

name: Each finding labeled by evidential status
definition: A finding does not say whether it is a confirmed error, likely, speculative/untested mechanism, alternative estimand or access limit, or mixes these types.
divergence: Three vocabularies: jaanch verdict refuted/confirmed/plausible + severity; assess-empirical-claims confirmed error/untested mechanism/alternative estimand/access limit; I4R CONFIRMED/LIKELY/SPECULATIVE with benign explanations listed and ruled out. audit-analysis uses speculative + rank buckets. No shared label set.
reason: Finding must carry an evidential-status label.

name: Each paper claim gets a support verdict
definition: A headline claim is not assigned Supported / Supported with narrower scope / Descriptive only / Unsupported, or an Unsupported verdict does not quote the claim and name the closest defensible replacement.
divergence: Only audit-analysis grades claims (not comments). jaanch grades comments, never the paper's claims.
reason: Each claim must get a fixed verdict label.

name: Reproduction or robustness outcome classified with reasons
definition: A reproduction is not classified (full / minor issues / partial / not reproducible, with reason) or a robustness reproduction does not report share of tests supporting the original, change in mean effect and sign/significance agreement.
divergence: No tool of ours uses the AEA or I4R outcome scheme; audit-analysis untestable_not_passed and assess access_scope_stated are partial.
reason: Reproduction outcome must use fixed classification.

name: Support/weaken criteria written before the grid runs
definition: The thresholds, signs or bounds that would support or weaken the headline are not written down before the robustness grid runs, or are changed afterwards.
divergence: Only audit-analysis tier3.
reason: Reviewer criteria fixed before robustness grid.

name: Each flag rated for importance to this paper
definition: A flag or candidate carries no severity/importance rating for the paper at hand, or the proposer's rating is accepted unreviewed.
divergence: jaanch uses two scales: completeness finder major/minor/negligible (negligible logged only) and comment severity critical/major/minor/suggestion, re-rated by the skeptic. AMICUS rates importance in a separate pass and uses it to weight a score. audit-analysis ranks by type bucket, not severity.
validation: AMICUS: 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text; repeat-coding correlation 0.84 for the universal score.
reason: Reviewer rates each flag's importance.

name: Findings ranked so consequential ones lead
definition: Findings are an unranked laundry list, immaterial concerns are manufactured, or requests are made that would not resolve a material uncertainty.
divergence: jaanch orders by severity then centrality to main_claims and caps the export at top ten; audit-analysis ranks by finding type (number-changing > inferential > identification > robustness > reproducibility > editorial > rejected > untestable) and must show the list before changing numbers; assess and write-referee prune at generation time rather than ranking after.
validation: jaanch strategies.md: a planted defect was generated but omitted from the capped top ten; the uncapped run placed it at material rank 15 (one stochastic rerun).
reason: Reviewer ordering of findings.

name: Merge duplicates without merging distinct problems
definition: Two comments reporting the same problem are both kept, or distinct problems sharing a quoted passage are merged.
divergence: jaanch editor merges by judgment (keep clearest quote, highest severity); the strict exporter treated shared quote as duplicate and rejected ranks 3 and 5, which concerned different assumptions. No other tool of ours dedupes explicitly.
validation: One observed failure in the editorial experiment (shared quote, different assumptions).
reason: Reviewer merging of duplicate comments.

name: Every candidate gets a verdict; rejected ones recorded
definition: A candidate has no verifier verdict, a refuted candidate reaches the report, or rejected findings and their reasons are discarded rather than recorded.
divergence: Conflict: jaanch drops refuted and unverdicted candidates from review.json (no rejected record in the output); audit-analysis requires rejected findings and the reason to be written down and ranked as a bucket. jaanch-experimental proposed keeping a full deduplicated record beside the top-ten list.
validation: Uncapped jaanch editor: 26 comments, 15 major, planted defect at rank 15 (lost from capped report).
reason: Every candidate must get a verdict; pipeline gate.

name: Every routed checklist item or section has a verdict
definition: A routed checklist item, tier section or headline question is silently skipped rather than given a finding or an explicit not-applicable/clean result.
divergence: jaanch enforces by script (checklists.jsonl must have exactly one valid row per check of every routed module; orchestrator reruns completeness once on problems). audit-analysis states the same rule for tiers and the four questions but has no script that checks the check matrix.
reason: Every routed checklist item gets a verdict.

name: Flagged checklist items reach the review
definition: A checklist item flagged major or minor does not appear as a comment naming its check id.
divergence: Substring match on check id only; negligible flags are logged but not reported.
reason: Flagged items compared with final review comments.

name: Overall summary consistent with the detailed comments
definition: The overall feedback cites a nonexistent comment, omits a critical comment, or a shortened summary drops or distorts a substantive point from the full list.
divergence: jaanch script checks cited ids exist but not the reverse (every critical comment cited is a prompt rule only). assess-empirical-claims checks retention of numbers, control-group context and limitation reasons by judgment.
reason: Review summary compared with detailed comments.

name: Checks not run and access limits stated
definition: A check that could not be run is reported as passed or omitted, a failed subagent goal is not reported, or the review does not state what was read and reproduced (e.g. claims full replication from selected tables).
divergence: audit-analysis requires 'untestable' with the missing artifact named; jaanch only reports a finder goal that failed twice and has no per-check untestable status in review.json (checklist rows have importance, not 'untestable'); assess and write-referee state access scope in prose.
reason: Review must disclose checks not run and scope.

name: Review sections cover the whole paper
definition: The paper is split into review sections whose line ranges leave gaps, so some text is never reviewed.
divergence: Prompt rule only; no script validates the ranges (could be one).
reason: Line-range arithmetic shows gaps in review coverage.

name: Paper routed to the checklists its own design uses
definition: A design checklist is applied to a paper that only cites the design, or omitted for one whose own analysis uses it; or a diagnostic is applied outside its supported design.
divergence: jaanch routes with a verbatim quote that is script-anchored (shows the quote exists, not that routing is right); AMICUS routes by LLM (mean 2.5 checklists per preprint); SciScore by guideline (CONSORT/ARRIVE/MDAR). assess-empirical-claims guards against misapplied diagnostics but does not route. Misrouting in jaanch silently removes checklist rows.
validation: AMICUS says routing 'is typically straightforward'; no error rate given.
reason: Choosing which design checklists apply to the paper.

name: Review artifacts validate against their schemas
definition: A comment, verdict, review, revision verdict or checklist file fails its JSON schema, has a duplicate id, or is not valid JSON.
divergence: jaanch only.
reason: Review artifacts validated against fixed schemas.

name: Every prior comment gets a revision verdict
definition: A comment of the prior review has no revision verdict in the recheck.
reason: Prior comments matched to revision verdicts.

name: Review tied to the exact paper reviewed
definition: The sha256 recorded in the review does not match the paper file given.
reason: Hash of reviewed file compared to recorded hash.

name: Untrusted manuscript ingested safely and faithfully
definition: The paper reads files outside the project root, the input format is unsupported, or macro expansion more than doubles the text.
reason: Ingest guards for the review pipeline.

name: Reviewer's own cited works and claims are real
definition: The reviewer suggests a work that cannot be confirmed by DOI/OpenAlex/arXiv/publisher page, cites from memory, invents a result, or calls an exploratory design preregistered.
divergence: jaanch requires the identifier in the message; assess-empirical-claims states the rule without a lookup step; write-referee-report and audit-analysis have no explicit guard on their own suggested citations.
reason: Reviewer's own citations verified externally.

name: Recommended remedy is possible and sufficient
definition: A comment telling authors to do X does not check that X is possible (e.g. against live documentation) and would resolve the problem.
divergence: write-referee-report asks for a 'feasible remedy' but no tool of ours verifies feasibility.
reason: Reviewer remedy checked against documentation.

name: Supportive and null results held to the same standard
definition: Diagnostics that support the paper are omitted while weakening ones are reported, or null results are judged by a different standard than positive ones.
divergence: jaanch has no rule to report supportive diagnostics; its comments are defects only.
reason: Reviewer applies equal standards to supportive and null results.

name: Verifier shown to catch planted invalid input
definition: A verification step is never tested on deliberately wrong input (invalid criticisms, perturbed certificates), so its pass rate carries no evidence.
divergence: functional-form-sensitivity perturbs a certificate on every run; jaanch only proposes negative controls (not implemented) despite the 135/136 result; audit-analysis has none for its validation pass.
validation: King & Worthington judge on planted false sentences: 258/258 caught, 0/258 false alarms (external benchmark of this idea).
reason: Verifier tested on planted bad input.

name: Every repair gated by a test seen to fail first
definition: A repair or diagnosis is committed without a permanent gate (row conservation, schemas, counts, headline estimates, provenance) watched to fail on the old system, before verification finished, or by patching one call site instead of the shared definition.
divergence: audit-analysis gates.py implements gates but does not require watching them fail; empirical-problem-solving requires fail-on-old/pass-on-new.
reason: Agent repairs must be gated by tests; workflow, not paper.

name: Substantive changes classified and surfaced
definition: A substantive change (universe, denominator, benchmark, model, uncertainty method, claim strength) is made inside a writing/visualization pass, or unresolved substantive decisions are buried among completed fixes.
reason: Agent's substantive changes in a writing pass surfaced.

name: Independent second reviewer or naive review compared
definition: No independent review (other model, separate reviewer, or open-ended naive pass) is obtained and compared against the primary review, or one reviewer's claim is adopted without checking disagreements.
divergence: design-analysis asks for an independent model review of the plan; jaanch-experimental tried a two-review ensemble with a verifying editor (detected both dev targets vs one, not selected); AMICUS uses a naive review as a coverage probe.
validation: AMICUS: 37% of checklist method flags unmatched by naive review; only 30% of naive issues match a method flag; naive review predicts publication about as well (10.6 pp vs 10.3 pp per SD).
reason: Primary review compared with an independent review.

name: Screen out non-papers and recycled work
definition: The submission is coursework, a partial draft, contains leftover AI prompts, or rewrites published work.
reason: Desk screen of the submission before review.

name: Prose result numbers match their source exhibit or output
definition: A result number in the prose (or a corrigendum/transcription) disagrees with the table, figure or generated output it reports: wrong value, column, row, sign or rounding, including stale near-miss values left after an artifact changed.
divergence: jaanch compares by model against map.json tables with exact match (table/column/row/sign/rounding) and resolves LaTeX macros first; audit-analysis has a LaTeX-only script (audit_provenance scoped) that flags only CLOSE-BUT-NOT-EQUAL values within 3% of a number in the cited table (staleness), and exits 2 if it cannot resolve citations, so a grossly wrong number (>3% off) is not caught by the script; write-empirical-paper checks only headline numbers and against regenerated output (rerun), not against the typeset tables; corrigendum extends to units, denominators and uncertainty of new prose. None of ours handles non-LaTeX (PDF/Word) by script.
validation: audit_provenance precise_only cut false positives on a real manuscript from 8 to 0 and re-found a known stale paragraph (audit-analysis SKILL.md L32, L127); tier1 check 4 called the most productive single check. External: SPOT best model recall 21.1% precision 6.1% on real data-inconsistency errata; Refine 8/10 on Dawes consistency category.
reason: Prose number disagrees with its source exhibit.

name: Every manuscript numeral traces to a source
definition: A numeral in the manuscript cannot be classified as generated output, macro, citation year or deliberate literal with a stated source (an orphan number).
divergence: audit-analysis counts numeric tokens and locates the producing exhibit/script output (automated for LaTeX by audit_provenance); write-empirical-paper requires a four-way classification (generated/macro/citation year/literal) with no script shipped, so it is model-run there.
validation: write-empirical-paper SKILL.md L85-91 anecdote: drift up to 8 pp, 2.6 pp in abstract direction.
reason: Numeral cannot be traced to any source.

name: Same quantity stated twice agrees everywhere
definition: A quantity or interval stated more than once (abstract vs body, results vs limitations, prose vs own table, caption vs figure) takes different values.
divergence: audit-analysis only; jaanch has no explicit repeated-quantity sweep (covered implicitly by text_vs_tables and summaries_match_results).
validation: audit-analysis example: one interval reported as 6.2-8.4, [6.20, 8.27], 6.2-8.3 (bug taxonomy 5b).
reason: Same quantity takes different values in two places.

name: Abstract, intro, conclusion match results sign, size, certainty
definition: The abstract, introduction or conclusion describes a result with a different sign, size or certainty than the results section reports.
divergence: Certainty component overlaps reasoning-finder overclaiming checks.
reason: Summary result differs from results section in sign, size or certainty.

name: No part of the paper contradicts another
definition: Two parts of the paper make incompatible statements (e.g., an assumption violated by a later method, table values contradicting stated theory, methods/setup inconsistent with reported results).
divergence: None of ours states this as a generic check; jaanch splits it into specific sub-checks (text_vs_tables, definitions, summaries, cross-references).
validation: Dawes benchmark: one planted internal-consistency error per paper across 10 psychology papers; Refine 8/10 on this category.
reason: Two parts of the paper make incompatible statements.

name: Implementation, code and theory describe the same object
definition: The algorithm, simulation, pseudocode, code or experiment parameters (incl. sample sizes) do not satisfy or implement what the theory/equations specify.
divergence: Ours exists only as a proposed (unpromoted) jaanch-experimental strategy that also reads repository code and keeps code-translation errors separate from manuscript errors; coarse is a production prompt on paper text only.
validation: FLAWS: 26/16 implementation errors in benchmark; best GPT-5 39.1% identification at k=10 overall.
reason: Code or simulation does not implement the stated theory.

name: Each term and symbol means one thing throughout
definition: A variable, symbol, sample or term is defined or used with different meanings in different places, or an equation uses notation inconsistently with its definition.
divergence: Overlaps jaanch writing finder ('defined differently in two places'). Complement of construct_name_stable (one thing, two names).
reason: Term or sample means different things in different places.

name: One construct carries one name across text and exhibits
definition: The same construct is labeled with different names in caption, axes, tables and manuscript (elegant variation suggesting different quantities).
divergence: Duplicated: write-empirical-paper scopes to the manuscript; visualize-evidence scopes to caption/axes/table/manuscript. Same rule, two homes; jaanch checks the converse (one name, two meanings).
reason: Same construct named differently; clarity problem.

name: N agrees across text, tables, exclusions and subgroup counts
definition: Sample sizes differ across text, tables and stated exclusions, or reported subgroup counts do not add up to the reported total.
divergence: jaanch is model-run and includes the exclusion flow; scrutiny add_up_to is deterministic but only sums counts. Overlaps UNI-DATA-01 sample-flow disclosure.
reason: Sample sizes disagree across text, tables, subgroups.

name: Significance stars agree with reported p or SE
definition: A table's significance stars do not match the p-value or coefficient/SE ratio reported for that cell under the stated star thresholds.
divergence: Only jaanch; model-run although fully deterministic from coef, SE and the table note's thresholds.
reason: Stars recomputed from reported p or coef/SE.

name: Internal references point to items saying what's claimed
definition: 'See Section 4' or 'Table 3 shows' points to a missing item or one that does not show what the text claims.
reason: Internal reference points to missing or wrong item.

name: Text claims about a figure match the plotted values
definition: What the text says a figure shows (levels, trends, crossings, values, N) differs from what is plotted, including axis limits that silently drop observations from the caption's N.
divergence: jaanch checks only if figure files are discovered and the model can view images, otherwise it refuses to guess; I4R pixel-measures plotted values and reruns code to find axis-clipped observations.
reason: Text description disagrees with plotted values.

name: Caption and notes match marks, intervals, samples
definition: A caption or note describes a different interval, sample, encoding or panel than the rendered exhibit shows, or the rendered exhibit has visible defects (clipping, wrong panel order, unreadable labels).
divergence: visualize-evidence bundles caption accuracy with rendering QA (clipping, whitespace, type size); write-empirical-paper limits to marks/intervals/samples/notes.
reason: Caption disagrees with rendered exhibit.

name: Plotted quantity is the construct the caption names
definition: The exhibit's code plots a different construct, denominator or statistical transform (smoothed, binned, normalized, aggregated) than the caption and prose name.
reason: Code computes a different quantity than caption names.

name: Table notes describe the estimator the code ran
definition: A table note describes a method (SE type, clustering, delta-method SE) that the producing code did not compute.
divergence: audit-analysis states it only as a bug-taxonomy example (8b) and checks by reading code; write-empirical-paper prevents it by generating the SE clause from the fitted object (se_note() in design-analysis/scripts/se_ladder.R).
validation: write-empirical-paper repo-layout.md L198: 126 of 128 estimation calls took a package default and every hand-typed note was wrong.
reason: Table note disagrees with what code computed.

name: Named statistic matches its label and computation
definition: A statistic is labeled as something it is not (mean called median, marginal called joint, count called share), judged from text or from the code computing it.
divergence: Two audit-analysis versions: tier1 judges from paper/tables; tier2 requires code and checks both directions.
reason: Statistic label disagrees with its computation.

name: Verbal claims match the tests they cite
definition: A qualitative statement ('not distinguishable', 'significantly larger') contradicts the p-value or estimate in the cited table.
validation: Example: age chi2(4)=3.1, p=.55 contradicted the limitations text (bug taxonomy 4b).
reason: Verbal conclusion contradicts the test it cites.

name: Prose narrates claim-relevant nulls in cited tables
definition: A claim-relevant coefficient in a cited table (typically a null or wrong-sign estimate) is omitted from the prose while siblings are narrated.
reason: Prose omits claim-relevant nulls in cited tables.

name: Compared quantities share a denominator and base unit
definition: A regression mixes outcome and regressors built on different denominators, or a counterfactual/residual measure uses a different base unit than the baseline it is compared with.
validation: Example A: -3.069 (p<.001) became -10.905 (p=.138); Example B: 84.3% -> 70.2% (tier1 check 1).
reason: Mixed denominators mean compared quantities measure different things.

name: Decomposition components sum to the headline estimand
definition: Components of a shift-share/Oaxaca decomposition do not sum to their total, or the total is not the same (weighting/unit) headline quantity it claims to decompose.
divergence: gates.assert_decomposition_reconciles checks only the internal sum; tier2 D also requires total == headline estimand, which no script checks.
reason: Decomposition components must sum to total.

name: Counterfactuals preserve mechanical accounting invariants
definition: A counterfactual that only reassigns a fixed set of units changes an invariant total (e.g., total income or education of fully matched people).
reason: Counterfactual breaking a mechanical invariant reveals a computation error.

name: OLS and IV compared on identical samples
definition: OLS and IV estimates are compared across different samples, outcomes, controls or units, or a large IV/OLS ratio is read as proof of bias without uncertainty.
reason: OLS-IV gap read as bias needs identical samples and uncertainty.

name: Analyses follow the preregistration or PAP
definition: Hypotheses, sample size, exclusions or analyses in the paper deviate from the preregistration/PAP (or are missing) without disclosure.
divergence: No row of ours in this category; jaanch:exp_report_02_prereg_primary_deviations (category reporting) checks that deviations are disclosed, not a dimension-by-dimension comparison with the registration.
reason: Paper compared to registered plan; undisclosed deviations.

name: Revision substantively fixes each prior comment
definition: A prior review comment is not substantively fixed in the revision (wording changed but the wrong number or problem remains, recomputation still fails, or the fix introduces a new error).
reason: Revision compared against prior review comments; review workflow.

name: Paper versions with same estimates report same derived quantities
definition: Two versions (or two robustness tables) with identical coefficients/log-likelihood report different derived quantities, or tables for different specifications are byte-identical (the change did not run).
divergence: Both are bug-taxonomy observations in audit-analysis, not stated rules; identical-table detection is trivially scriptable but no script exists.
reason: Versions with same estimates report different derived numbers.

name: Encodings and table conventions consistent across exhibits
definition: The same concept is encoded with different colors/shapes across figures, or tables differ in precision, caption style, missing-value symbol or note structure.
reason: Encodings and table conventions inconsistent across exhibits.

name: Panels compared in prose share axes
definition: Panels the prose compares use independent scales (unsignaled) so apparent differences are manufactured.
divergence: visualize-evidence says check programmatically where possible, but no script exists.
reason: Unsignaled independent scales manufacture visual differences.

name: Visual differences proportional to data differences
definition: A truncated, nonlinear, area or 3-D encoding makes visual differences disproportionate to data differences (Tufte lie factor).
reason: Lie-factor convention for proportional encoding.

name: Displayed ordering matches current data values
definition: A figure's visual order or a table's row order/rounding asserts a ranking the current values contradict (stale or hand-set order).
divergence: visualize-evidence checks figures against data; write-empirical-paper checks tables and demands order be computed from values in code.
reason: Displayed order contradicts current values.

name: Every plot aesthetic traces to a variable or constant
definition: A plot aesthetic mapping cannot be traced to a named variable or deliberate constant in the code.
reason: Every aesthetic must trace to a variable; provenance rule.

name: Each headline claim traces end to end
definition: A headline claim cannot be traced through estimand, analytic universe, unit/denominator, source data, cleaning rule, producing script, artifact, uncertainty method and manuscript locations, or a conflict along the chain is unrecorded.
divergence: Overlaps assess-empirical-claims claim_evidence_trace (other category).
reason: Claim chain from estimand to manuscript has breaks or conflicts.

name: One code path per shared computation
definition: Two code paths compute the same quantity or style and can drift apart.
reason: Duplicate code paths can drift and misreport.

name: Generated table fragments exclude captions
definition: A generated table fragment embeds float/caption/label, so regenerating it can silently change the caption.
divergence: Repository convention rather than a check of a paper's content.
reason: Generated fragments must exclude captions; pipeline convention.

name: Test statistic and df imply reported p
definition: The p-value recomputed from a reported test statistic and degrees of freedom does not match the reported p (allowing rounding), including decision errors where they fall on opposite sides of the threshold.
divergence: jaanch runs it by model with Python on any test, in text or tables, with no restriction or validation; statcheck parses only APA-formatted text (misses tables); metacheck restricts to t and F tests because other types were not validated. jaanch does not separately flag decision errors.
validation: metacheck stat_check validation: 685 APA t/F tests, 34/34 true inconsistencies found, 26 false flags (43% of flags false). Dawes: Nuijten reports 12.5% of papers with gross inconsistencies.
reason: p recomputed from statistic and df.

name: Coefficient, SE, t, p and CI imply each other
definition: A reported coefficient, its SE, t statistic, p-value and confidence interval are mutually inconsistent (e.g., CI not coef +/- 1.96 SE, t != coef/SE).
divergence: Only jaanch, model-run with Python; no deterministic script exists in ours or external rows (statcheck needs APA strings).
reason: Coef, SE, t, p, CI recomputed against each other.

name: Percentages, differences, ratios and shares recompute
definition: A percentage, difference, ratio, sum, share or 'X times' claim does not equal what its reported inputs give at the reported precision (a percentage not reconstructible from paper numbers when code is silent).
divergence: jaanch flags any mismatch; assess-empirical-claims explicitly says missing code alone is not failure and tries reconstruction from the paper; scrutiny percentage_of additionally searches nearby denominators to diagnose a benign cause (valid responses, pre-attrition n) - none of ours does that denominator search.
validation: Dawes benchmark: best single system 71/100 overall across categories; Black Spatula ~10% wrong-error rate from secondary press (unverified).
reason: Derived percentages and ratios recomputed.

name: Equations and derivations re-derive correctly
definition: Re-deriving an equation (by hand, exact arithmetic or symbolic algebra) gives a different sign, order, constant or impossible limit that affects a stated result, shown by a concrete numerical instance.
divergence: jaanch-experimental proposal (unpromoted; production reasoning finder already asks for sympy rechecks - other category); coarse requires a concrete numerical instantiation of any claimed error, which ours does not state.
reason: Re-derived equation gives a different result; derivation logic.

name: Mean of integer data is possible given n
definition: No integer total k gives k/(n*items) rounding to the reported mean (or percentage) at its reported decimals (GRIM).
divergence: jaanch runs GRIM by model with Python and does not state the preconditions (integer data, number of items averaged, decimals); scrutiny's grim implementation is deterministic.
reason: GRIM test on reported means.

name: Mean, SD, n feasible for bounded or binary data
definition: No sample of the reported n with the scale's bounds (or binary 0/1 values) can produce the reported mean and SD at their precision (GRIMMER, DEBIT, bounded mean-SD test).
divergence: No version of ours.
reason: GRIMMER/DEBIT feasibility on mean, SD, n.

name: A plausible integer sample matches reported statistics
definition: Searching for integer samples with the reported n, mean, SD and bounds finds none, or only implausible ones (SPRITE heuristic, CLOSURE exhaustive).
divergence: No version of ours.
reason: SPRITE/CLOSURE sample reconstruction.

name: Subgroup summary statistics reconcile with whole sample
definition: Subgroup means/SDs/ns cannot combine to the reported whole-sample statistics.
divergence: No version of ours (jaanch derived_numbers covers sums only).
reason: Subgroup statistics must combine to whole.

name: Reported effect size matches its test statistic
definition: A reported Cohen's d, g, partial eta-squared or omega-squared matches none of the standard formulas applied to the reported statistic and df.
divergence: No version of ours.
validation: metacheck: coherence correctly indicated for 218/221 Cohen's d and 480/485 partial eta-squared.
reason: Effect size recomputed from test statistic.

name: Reported correlation matrix is a possible matrix
definition: A reported correlation table is not internally consistent (cannot be a valid correlation matrix, likely positive semi-definiteness).
divergence: No version of ours.
reason: Correlation matrix must be positive semidefinite.

name: Reported statistics lie within attainable bounds
definition: A reported statistic is algebraically or procedurally impossible: p outside [0,1], p below the floor attainable with B permutation draws, CR < AVE, or similar sign/bound violations.
divergence: audit-analysis covers only the randomization-inference p floor (B=200 -> min p .005); metacheck only p outside [0,1]; I4R lists a broader set of no-data anomalies (CR<AVE, sign errors, required n rounded down).
reason: Reported statistic outside attainable bounds.

name: Focal contrast summed from all relevant coefficients
definition: The claim rests on a single coefficient when the relevant contrast is a sum of main effect and interactions (with covariance terms for its SE).
validation: Worked example: Anderson Table 4(2) -88 + 851 = 763 (review-moves line 17).
reason: Contrast and its SE need all relevant coefficients and covariances.

name: Joint 'all of' claims bounded by marginals
definition: An 'all of' (joint) share exceeds the smallest marginal or was read off a marginal.
validation: Example: 65% claimed, joint 59.1% (bug taxonomy 5a).
reason: Joint share cannot exceed smallest marginal.

name: Coefficients translated into natural units are plausible
definition: Translating a coefficient or standardized effect into implied counts, totals, dollars, years or population quantities (with numerator and denominator) yields values beyond physical bounds or best external evidence.
divergence: Three phrasings inside audit-analysis (SKILL.md plausibility, two paper-audit adversarial bullets); same move.
reason: Implied natural-unit magnitude implausible; signals overreading or error.

name: Implied treatment-on-treated effect is plausible
definition: Dividing the ITT by plausible or measured compliance/exposure (or computing the implied elasticity/counterfactual rate) gives an implausible effect against benchmarks.
divergence: Three copies in audit-analysis: move 6 and the adversarial bullet use 'plausible' exposure; tier4 RCT branch requires 'measured' compliance.
reason: Implied effect on treated implausible against benchmarks.

name: Control mean reconstructed into counts per 100
definition: The control-group mean's numerator, denominator, missingness, weighting, respondent, question and window cannot be recovered or, translated into counts per 100 eligible units, is implausible.
reason: Control mean's construction must be recoverable; then plausibility judged.

name: Numerator over rate reconstructs the intended denominator
definition: For a rate, numerator/rate does not return the denominator expected, or different compared rate columns use different denominators.
divergence: Three strictness levels in audit-analysis: tier1 prose rule; audit_data.denominators only warns (soft) and needs a numerator column named as the rate stem; gates.assert_same_denominator raises on mismatch or impossible reconstruction.
validation: Example C: residual summed to exactly 60,547 (tier1 check 1).
reason: Numerator over rate must return stated denominator.

name: Topline change decomposed into within-group and mix
definition: A topline change attributed to a real effect is instead a composition (mix) shift, shown when every segment moves the other way (Simpson's paradox).
reason: Composition shift masquerades as an effect (Simpson's paradox).

name: WTP averaging named and denominator zero-crossing checked
definition: WTP is reported without naming ratio-of-means vs mean-of-ratios vs median (all three not shown), or the denominator coefficient crosses zero within the covariate range for a nontrivial sample share.
validation: Bug taxonomy 8a: mean -10.5/-13.2/-21.4 vs median ~-10.3; 8c zero crossing 0.25 above mean SES.
reason: WTP averaging rule and zero-crossing denominator affect estimate.

name: Break-even scenarios use observed or labeled inputs
definition: A break-even or profitability scenario uses invented prices, quantities or recoverable profits not labeled hypothetical.
reason: Invented inputs presented as observed in break-even scenario.

name: Join key unique; key transform injective
definition: A key that must be unique has duplicate rows, or a normalization of the key (case folding, substitution, truncation) collapses distinct values.
divergence: audit_data.shape_and_keys only checks uniqueness when --key is passed and skips otherwise; gates.py has the injective-transform test but audit_data.py does not.
reason: Duplicate or collapsing keys found in data.

name: Merge cardinality declared; no many-to-many
definition: A merge does not declare its cardinality and expected row count, or neither side is unique so rows multiply and silently reweight downstream means.
divergence: Prose only. No script greps for merges lacking validate=/assert; gates.assert_row_conservation catches the symptom only if the author calls it.
reason: Undeclared many-to-many merge multiplies rows.

name: Row counts conserved across every operation
definition: A merge, filter, groupby or reshape changes the row count unexpectedly, including units vanishing when a filtered frame is grouped and assigned back.
divergence: The gate only fires where called; the groupby-on-filtered-frame pattern is a code-reading (grep) candidate with no script.
validation: audit-analysis worked example: 288 of 13,711 vs 472 of 12,748 pages lost; stability claim moved -0.1pp -> -0.8pp.
reason: Row counts change unexpectedly across operations.

name: Raw records traced to analysis sample
definition: Cleaning, joins, exclusions, recodes, weights or preprocessing between raw data and the analysis sample introduce an unexplained row change, duplicate, unit/scale conflict, leakage or unambiguous coding error.
divergence: assess-empirical-claims traces to model matrices and reported samples; write-empirical-paper defers detail to audit-analysis; I4R makes it a precondition (fix coding errors before robustness). ScholScan is a broad benchmark category (text-only) rather than a procedure.
reason: Raw-to-analysis pipeline introduces unexplained changes.

name: Missing values not silently filled as zero
definition: Not-measured values are filled with zero (explicit fills or NaN-swallowing comparisons like x > 0), so measured-zero, positive and not-measured are indistinguishable, or an unavailable/undefined statistic is reported as a real zero.
divergence: audit-analysis demands a three-state observed flag in the data (gated); audit_data.zeros_vs_missing only counts zeros vs NAs and asks; corrigendum adds a fourth state (mathematically undefined) and warns deletion is not uniquely correct. The grep patterns are listed in prose, not scripted.
validation: audit-analysis examples: -8.7pp vs true -3.1pp; 49.1% vs 74.2%. Tier1 check 2 called the second most productive bug class.
reason: Missing coded as zero conflates measured and unmeasured.

name: Missingness or attrition differs by group/period
definition: Missing data, row loss or attrition differs across arms, waves, groups, exposure or outcome predictors (or overall attrition is high), manufacturing trends or bias.
divergence: audit_data flags max-min fill-rate gap > 2pp by --group only; prose asks for every grouping variable and every period; the selection branch adds exposure and outcome predictors. Dawes uses >20% overall attrition as a threshold none of ours has, and works from paper text, not data.
validation: Dawes benchmark: one planted attrition error per paper, 10 psychology papers; best single system 71/100 overall (not per category).
reason: Differential missingness or attrition biases comparisons.

name: Missing data, exclusions, outliers, transforms disclosed
definition: The paper does not report amount and mechanism of missing data, how it was handled, post-collection exclusion criteria, outlier rules or transformations.
divergence: No row of ours in these categories checks disclosure from text; ours check the data itself (differential_missingness). May be covered under 'reporting' elsewhere.
reason: Required disclosure of missing data, exclusions, transforms.

name: Sample flow and N per analysis documented
definition: Numbers at each stage (randomized/eligible, treated, analysed), losses with reasons, per-variable missingness, weights/strata, or model-specific N and clusters are missing or differ across models without explanation.
divergence: CONSORT (trials) and STROBE (observational) are disclosure items from text; assess-empirical-claims records N, clusters, weights from code/data per estimate.
reason: Required stage-by-stage N and losses by group.

name: Values within logical and scale bounds
definition: A bounded quantity is out of range: shares outside [0,1], negative counts, dates outside the window, responses outside the scale, subscale scores above maximum, impossible demographics.
divergence: audit_data.ranges uses column-name heuristics (share/pct/count/n_) and does not check dates; gates.assert_bounded needs explicit bounds. I4R uses scale/codebook maxima and traces whether bad values entered published statistics; ours does not read a codebook.
reason: Values outside logical bounds in data.

name: Dtype traps after merges (bool-object, pd.NA)
definition: A boolean column becomes object after a merge (so ~ is bitwise NOT) or pd.NA makes a numeric column object so describe() reports the wrong statistic.
divergence: pandas-specific; no R/Stata equivalent anywhere.
validation: audit-analysis bug taxonomy 7b: 1,120 distinct values reported as mean; true 11.70.
reason: Dtype changes after merge corrupt computations.

name: Every dataset profiled before modeling
definition: Datasets are modeled without profiling shape, column types, missingness, zeros, ranges, skew, tail mass and leverage; heavy skew unaddressed in estimator choice.
divergence: Prose asks for kurtosis and a plot; audit_data.distributions has neither (|skew|>2 or max/median>20). metacheck profiles column type/measurement level/constant columns but has no skew threshold.
validation: metacheck: not validated.
reason: Unprofiled skew and leverage unaddressed in estimator choice.

name: Duplicate rows defined by entity, not coincidence
definition: Exact, near or block-duplicated rows inflate the sample, or conversely legitimate repeated observations are dropped because duplicates were defined by repeated IDs or matching low-dimensional response profiles.
divergence: Opposite emphasis: I4R/scrutiny/sequence tools hunt duplicates (incl. offset blocks) as inflation or fabrication evidence; corrigendum and write-empirical-paper warn against over-calling duplicates. None of ours is scripted.
validation: scrutiny: no published validation.
reason: Duplicate rows inflate or wrongly shrink sample.

name: Statistical signatures of fabricated data
definition: Data or reported numbers show signatures of fabrication: absent latent structure, uniform distributions with sharp cutoffs, implausibly narrow ranges, non-Benford leading digits, condition means more linear than sampling allows.
divergence: No equivalent in ours. audit-analysis anomalous_level_trace explicitly says an extreme rate alone establishes neither error nor fabrication.
reason: Statistical signatures of fabricated numbers.

name: Figures reused or manipulated
definition: An image or figure panel is reused or manipulated across the paper.
validation: SPOT: 27 of 91 errors; best model o3 recall 21.1%, precision 6.1% (all categories).
reason: Reused or manipulated figure panels.

name: No personal data in replication deposit
definition: The deposit contains names, DOB, emails, IPs, geolocation, IDs, identifying free text or metadata, or unique per-person combinations, whether or not anonymization was claimed.
divergence: AEA uses J-PAL PII-Scan (script); I4R adds per-person uniqueness and filenames/metadata.
reason: Deposit scanned against fixed list of identifier types.

name: Anomalous control levels traced to source
definition: An unusual control/baseline level or drift within the control regime is not decomposed by cohort, period, time at risk and strata and traced to coding and original responses.
divergence: audit-analysis classifies the outcome (coding error / construct mismatch / corroborated / unresolved); assess-empirical-claims only asks for time variation.
reason: Anomalous baseline traced to coding and source responses.

name: Instrumentation or deploy change at discontinuity
definition: A metric moved because logging, instrumentation, config, schema, bot filter or dashboard definitions changed at that time, not because the world changed.
reason: Metric moved from instrumentation change, not the construct.

name: Sample ratio mismatch in assignment counts
definition: Observed assignment counts reject the intended allocation ratio (chi-square), meaning assignment, execution or a join is broken.
divergence: Listed as a model step; the chi-square is trivially scriptable from reported arm counts but no script exists in ours.
validation: Skill claims SRM in ~6% of online experiments (unsourced in row).
reason: Assignment counts reject intended allocation; randomization broken.

name: Data keeps dimensions/items needed for diagnosis
definition: Data were pre-aggregated (e.g. totals without items) so the cause, miscoding, differential item functioning or component dominance cannot be seen.
reason: Pre-aggregated data hide miscoding and item functioning.

name: Upstream estimates not rounded before reuse
definition: A generated quantity is rounded or stored at reduced precision before entering a downstream regression.
reason: Rounded generated quantity distorts downstream regression.

name: Geographic joins use a verified crosswalk
definition: External geographic data are joined on coincidentally similar codes without a verified crosswalk and boundary-change audit.
reason: Geographic join without verified crosswalk mismatches units.

name: Count observations a suspected bug touches
definition: A result is attributed to a coding error without counting affected analysis rows in the right unit (respondents, groups, group-issue pairs, cells) and re-estimating.
divergence: assess-empirical-claims counts to test attribution; corrigendum counts for reporting and insists on unit and on revised vs historical counts.
validation: assess-empirical-claims example: caste-recoding typo changes zero pairs.
reason: Bug attribution requires counting affected rows and re-estimating.

name: Fix leaves unaffected rows and near misses unchanged
definition: A fix alters pre-existing rows (values or NA pattern) or regresses near-miss cases that were already correct.
divergence: audit-analysis demands bit-identical pre-existing rows; empirical-problem-solving samples near misses deliberately instead of checking all rows.
reason: Fix must not alter unaffected rows.

name: Missing/suppressed cells visible on maps
definition: Sparse, missing, suppressed or uncertain cells are drawn like observed ones, no support rule is defined, or observations lacking coordinates are not counted.
reason: Missing cells drawn like observed ones on maps.

name: Rerun reproduces published numbers at printed precision
definition: Running the original code on the original data does not reproduce a table cell, figure, coefficient, SE, N or percentage at the precision printed (or the committed artifact).
divergence: Comparison target differs: audit-analysis diffs against committed artifacts (any diff fails); AEA/I4R compare to the manuscript cell by cell at printed precision; assess-empirical-claims restricts to decisive numbers; functional-form-sensitivity compares to a template baseline and reports the gap to the paper. No tool of ours states a numeric tolerance. script_exists=true only because metacheck executes code (it does not compare outputs to the paper).
validation: Reviewer3 on Dawes benchmark: 30/100 planted errors caught (all categories).
reason: Rerunning original code must reproduce published numbers.

name: Number re-derived independently from producing code
definition: Re-deriving a reported number by a second route from the code that produced it (not its description) gives a different value.
reason: Second route from code gives a different number.

name: Design-based ITT reproduced from assignment
definition: The ITT computed from the known assignment mechanism (with design-based inference) does not match the reported estimate.
reason: ITT recomputed from known assignment must match report.

name: Every prose number produced by code
definition: A number in the text appears in no generated artifact or code output (hand-computed or typed), so it cannot be regenerated.
divergence: audit_provenance matches number strings against any artifact value (excluding years and small integers), so coincidental matches pass; AEA requires a page/line-to-code trace; write-empirical-paper enforces prevention via generated macros.
reason: Prose number absent from generated outputs.

name: Claims trace to exhibit, script and output
definition: A claim, number, table or figure cannot be traced through exhibit, producing script, sample and variable definition, or the chain includes manual transcription or live downloads.
divergence: write-empirical-paper relies on an Output header convention in its R/LaTeX template; audit-analysis builds a dependency inventory; assess-empirical-claims traces per claim. None scripted.
reason: Claim cannot be traced through exhibit, script, output.

name: Tables and figures generated from one computed source
definition: A table body is hand-maintained rather than a generated fragment, or a table and a figure compute the same quantity separately and can disagree.
validation: write-empirical-paper motivating case: six hand-kept rows drifted up to 8 pp.
reason: Exhibits must be generated from one source.

name: Committed artifacts not stale relative to inputs
definition: A table or figure is older than the data/code it derives from, shown by timestamps or by reproducing the committed table from pre-fix data.
divergence: Timestamps are a candidate signal (confirm against git history); bit-for-bit reproduction of the old table is the proof.
validation: audit-analysis bug taxonomy 4c: +21.0% published vs +22.2% current.
reason: Committed artifacts older than inputs.

name: Shipped code parses and runs on another machine
definition: The code fails to parse or run as shipped: undeclared dependencies, absolute paths, setwd/install.packages, placeholder paths, runtime fetches, locale parsing, wrong data paths, or existing tests/compile already failing.
divergence: metacheck scripts static and sandboxed execution (R/Python only); ours only has write-empirical-paper's 'run existing tests and compile' on the author's own repo, no portability checks.
validation: metacheck: not validated.
reason: Shipped code fails to run.

name: Data and files the code loads are deposited
definition: Analysis data files, files the code reads, or linked repositories are missing or unresolvable without a stated reason.
divergence: metacheck warns even when data legitimately cannot be shared; AEA accepts a stated reason.
validation: metacheck repo_listing: error rates unknown.
reason: Required data and files missing from deposit.

name: One main script runs the whole package
definition: No main/master file calls all other programs in order.
reason: Replication package lacks a master script.

name: Software, versions, compute and seeds recorded
definition: OS, software versions, compute and runtime are not stated, package versions are unpinned (no lockfile/sessionInfo/date pin), or seeds are unrecorded.
divergence: metacheck checks R lockfiles only; write-empirical-paper bundles seeds with renv pinning (R template); AEA also records the replicator's environment.
reason: Required environment, versions, seeds unrecorded.

name: Bootstrap RNG created inside function
definition: A module-level RNG consumed across calls makes published intervals depend on execution order.
reason: Module-level RNG makes intervals order-dependent.

name: Estimator defaults and dependency changes checked
definition: Results depend on function arguments left at defaults, or pinned dependencies changed defaults across versions, and varying them flips conclusions.
reason: Conclusion flips with estimator defaults or versions.

name: Analysis code commented
definition: Code files contain no comments.
validation: metacheck: not validated.
reason: Code readability; uncommented code.

name: Code implements the stated method and controls
definition: The code does not implement the method the paper states, e.g. a claimed control never enters the fitted model.
reason: Code does not implement stated method.

name: Pipeline recovers planted parameters or known answers
definition: Run end to end on simulated data with known parameters, or an algorithm on small cases with known answers, the pipeline misses the truth beyond Monte Carlo error.
divergence: gates.assert_recovers_known_truth tests bias within tol + 2 MC SEs; tier4 prose adds interval coverage the gate does not test; assess-empirical-claims applies it to matching/equilibrium algorithms with hand-built cases.
reason: Pipeline fails to recover planted truth.

name: Regression estimates enter simulation unchanged
definition: The structural simulation does not use the published estimates as claimed: sample, weights, coefficient order, category meanings, signs, missingness or units differ.
reason: Simulation does not use published estimates as claimed.

name: Correction compares published and corrected at same precision
definition: A corrected value's difference from the published one is misstated (different units, denominators, samples, weights or uncertainty).
reason: Published-vs-corrected difference misstated.

name: Paper compiles clean; exhibits checked rendered
definition: The build has unresolved citations/references, missing assets or overfull content, or a figure was judged only as a standalone asset rather than at delivery size.
divergence: Arguably writing/presentation rather than reproduction; kept here because both rows require regenerating and compiling.
reason: Build errors and rendered exhibit defects.

name: Each headline claim mapped to an estimand
definition: A headline claim cannot be tied to a unit, population, treatment, outcome, comparison, aggregation, weighting and time window.
divergence: Only audit-analysis builds an explicit claim-to-estimand table; jaanch's reasoning finder asks the estimand question per section without a table.
reason: Headline claim not tied to an estimand.

name: Design identifies the estimand the paper claims
definition: The comparison actually made (estimator, sample, population, weighting) is not the one the claim is about.
divergence: audit-analysis Q2 also checks the checkable assumptions; jaanch reasoning finder is section-local and reports only problems in its section, so a design/claim mismatch spanning sections can be missed.
validation: Refine scored 2/10 on causal-inference planted errors in Dawes benchmark.
reason: Comparison made is not the one claimed.

name: Alternative analyses compared on estimand and assumptions
definition: Analytical alternatives are compared on results without first stating each one's estimand, usable data and identifying assumptions.
reason: Alternatives compared without estimands and assumptions.

name: Causal claim names and defends its assumptions
definition: A causal claim from non-experimental data does not name the assumptions that make it causal, what would violate them, and a reason to believe each.
divergence: jaanch flags silence (if_silent=flag) on any observational causal claim; design-analysis additionally requires stating which implications are checkable, an ex-ante bar.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text. (jaanch item quoted from AMICUS universal list)
reason: Causal claim must name and defend its assumptions.

name: Concrete failure scenario per assumption addressed
definition: For a key assumption there is a simple concrete way it fails, and the paper neither acknowledges nor bounds the resulting bias.
divergence: No tool of ours constructs a failure scenario per assumption; design-analysis only asks 'what would violate it'.
reason: Concrete assumption failure neither acknowledged nor bounded.

name: Assumption contradicted by the paper's own evidence
definition: A stated assumption is contradicted by the paper's own data, design or examples.
divergence: Partly covered by audit-analysis Q2 ('checks the checkable ones') but not as an explicit cross-reading of assumptions against the paper's own exhibits.
reason: Stated assumption contradicted by paper's own data.

name: Causal language matches what the design supports
definition: Effect/impact/causes language is used for a conditional association whose exchangeability is not defended.
divergence: jaanch splits this from UNI-IDENT-01 (missing assumptions); audit-analysis frames it as 'adjustment identifies a conditional association' only for cross-sections.
validation: Dawes: causal-inference category among hardest; Refine caught 2/10.
reason: Causal language for undefended associations.

name: Identification not argued from controls, FE, fit, balance
definition: Identification is inferred from controls, fixed effects, predictive fit, balance or a small p-value rather than from a located source of variation.
divergence: Same wording in both; design-analysis adds the remedy (state the descriptive quantity the data do support).
reason: Identification argued from controls or fit, not variation.

name: No post-treatment or mediator controls without justification
definition: A control that could be caused by treatment (mediator, collider, downstream response) is adjusted for as if pre-determined, changing the estimand without comment.
divergence: audit-analysis excludes post-treatment controls 'unless the estimand justifies them' and asks for a DAG only in the cross-section branch; assess-empirical-claims says do not 'automatically' control them away (both directions are errors); design-analysis uses DAG 'where it clarifies'. Threshold for what counts as justified differs.
reason: Post-treatment controls bias the estimate.

name: Analytic sample selection and conditioning disclosed
definition: The estimand silently conditions on an outcome or on selection into the analytic sample (complete cases, response, inner join), changing the population described.
divergence: Three audit-analysis tiers (tier2 B, tier2 D, tier4 selection) state the same check; only left_vs_inner inspects code.
reason: Conditioning on selection changes population and biases estimate.

name: Sensitivity to unmeasured confounding quantified
definition: A selection-on-observables causal estimate has no sensitivity analysis (E-value, Cinelli-Hazlett robustness value, Rosenbaum bounds).
divergence: jaanch flags absence from text (severity medium); audit-analysis computes it from data (rerun). AMICUS applies it universally to any observational estimate.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text. Flagged on 95% of applicable preprints.
reason: No sensitivity to unmeasured confounding.

name: Position on spillovers between units stated and supported
definition: An effect estimate ignores plausible interference/spillovers or heterogeneous treatment versions that invalidate the comparison or ITT quotient.
divergence: AMICUS universal (every effect estimate); audit-analysis only in RCT branch, bundled with blocking and pre-outcome covariate choice; assess only for ITT quotients. jaanch has no spillover item despite citing AMICUS.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text. Flagged on 92%.
reason: Spillovers violate SUTVA.

name: Placebo and balance checks able to fail
definition: Placebo/balance/negative-control variables could themselves be treatment consequences or could not change the interpretation.
divergence: I4R reruns supportive analyses; assess checks causal timing of placebos; design-analysis is ex-ante; audit-analysis uses within-control change as an implicit placebo.
reason: Placebo or balance check unable to fail.

name: Bounds reported when point identification fails
definition: A point estimate is reported as though identification were complete when selection or missing outcomes call for Manski/Lee-type bounds.
divergence: Tier3 (model, text) and tier4 (rerun) versions of the same check inside audit-analysis.
reason: Bounds needed when point identification fails.

name: Coefficient not identified by a handful of observations
definition: A coefficient exists but its independent variation comes from very few observations.
reason: Coefficient identified by very few observations.

name: Result robust to reasonable functional forms
definition: The estimate depends on the published functional form; bins, splines, logs or raw/partial plots tell a different story.
reason: Estimate depends on functional form.

name: Linear predictions stay inside bounded outcome range
definition: A linear model of a bounded outcome predicts outside its bounds where interpretation depends on them.
reason: Linear predictions exit bounded outcome range.

name: Dose response shown across every exposure level
definition: The effect is isolated in one exposure cell rather than a smooth relationship, and only the binary contrast is shown.
reason: Dose-response not shown across exposure levels.

name: Mechanism links measured and rivals considered
definition: A mechanism is asserted with neither the treatment->mediator nor mediator->outcome link measured, or a total effect is read as a mechanism's contribution.
divergence: jaanch-experimental version (proposed, not promoted) counts only when the paper makes the stronger mechanism claim; assess also demands a rival mechanism.
reason: Mechanism asserted without measured links.

name: Two admissible mechanisms give same data
definition: Two admissible data-generating processes produce the same observed distribution but different targets, demonstrating nonidentification.
divergence: Experimental only; bar is demonstrated nonidentification, not possible confounding.
reason: Observationally equivalent DGPs with different targets.

name: Cause tested by removal and by injection
definition: A diagnosed cause is supported only by removal from a failing case, or the injected effect is too small to explain the symptom.
reason: Causal diagnosis of a bug needs removal and injection tests.

name: Broad 'methodology problems' category (no specific test)
definition: Catch-all category in external reviewers/benchmarks for methodology or experimental-design flaws with no operational definition.
validation: Dawes: best single system 71/100 planted errors, all 7 never-caught are omissions. SPOT: best model recall 21.1%, precision 6.1%. Stanford: Spearman with humans 0.42.
reason: Generic methodology-flaw category; design supports claim.

name: AMICUS survey-experiment checklist (items unpublished)
definition: Placeholder for AMICUS's 18-item survey-experiment checklist whose item text is not quoted.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: AMICUS survey-experiment design checklist.

name: AMICUS conjoint checklist (items unpublished)
definition: Placeholder for AMICUS's 5-item conjoint checklist whose item text is not quoted.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: AMICUS conjoint design checklist.

name: Randomization procedure described and verified
definition: Sequence generation, allocation concealment, who assigned, and the realized assignment (delivery, noncompliance, outcome collection by arm) are not described or verified.
divergence: CONSORT asks for the procedure to be reported; audit-analysis verifies realized assignment from data and also bundles delivery and attrition.
reason: Randomization procedure described and verified.

name: Treatment delivered and measured as described
definition: No receipts, spot checks, manipulation checks or records show the intervention (or apparatus) happened as described and outcomes were gathered.
divergence: audit-analysis move5 also searches the web for later evidence; I4R checks a model/apparatus component against its spec in code.
reason: Manipulation checks show treatment is what was claimed.

name: Attrition by arm tested and bounded
definition: Attrition differs by arm and the estimate is not bounded (Lee/Manski).
reason: Differential attrition by arm must be bounded.

name: Blinding and masking reported and evaluated
definition: Who was masked to condition (participants, administrators, assessors), how, and whether masking succeeded are not reported.
reason: Blinding and its success reported.

name: Adjustment covariates pre-treatment and pre-specified
definition: Adjustment covariates are post-randomization, chosen after seeing imbalance, or too many (Green: M/20).
reason: Post-randomization or data-chosen covariates bias and add flexibility.

name: AMICUS field-experiment checklist (items unpublished)
definition: Placeholder for AMICUS's 20-item field-experiment checklist whose item text is not quoted.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: AMICUS field-experiment checklist.

name: IV: relevance, independence, exclusion, monotonicity defended separately
definition: IV assumptions are conflated, e.g. a strong first stage or historical origin offered as evidence of exogeneity.
divergence: audit-analysis lists four assumptions incl. monotonicity; assess lists heterogeneity/LATE and names the strong-first-stage fallacy.
reason: IV assumptions conflated.

name: IV: every instrument-to-outcome path audited
definition: Exclusion is asserted without tabulating known alternative pathways (timing, evidence, whether controls block them).
divergence: assess builds an explicit pathway table with web evidence; audit-analysis lists paths.
reason: Exclusion paths not audited.

name: IV: overid or balance tests not offered as exclusion
definition: Hansen J/Sargan or balance tests are cited as establishing exclusion, or post-instrument controls are added to 'fix' it.
reason: Overid tests do not establish exclusion; fixed rule.

name: IV: direct effect needed to overturn result quantified
definition: An exclusion concern is raised with no magnitude, or a one-at-a-time bound is presented as joint (Conley plausibly-exogenous style).
reason: Exclusion violation magnitude needed to overturn.

name: IV: complier population and margin of the LATE stated
definition: The population and margin represented by the LATE are not stated.
reason: LATE complier population and margin must be stated.

name: IV: generated-instrument regression sequence drawn out
definition: With generated instruments or interactions, an endogenous product is left uninstrumented or the construction imposes a hidden restriction.
reason: Generated instruments leave endogeneity or hidden restriction.

name: IV/encouragement: ToT uses the study's own first stage
definition: An ITT is divided by an exposure/compliance rate from another setting, or exposure, awareness and compliance are interchanged, and the quotient called an identified ToT.
