reason: ToT must use study's own first stage.

name: AMICUS IV checklist (items unpublished)
definition: Placeholder for AMICUS's 11-item IV checklist whose item text is not quoted.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: AMICUS IV checklist.

name: DiD: parallel trends stated and defended
definition: A DiD/event-study estimate never names parallel trends, or lacks group-by-time data to support a pre/post comparison (e.g. election cohorts alone).
divergence: jaanch: stated (text silence = flag, severity high); audit-analysis: requires a credible argument plus supporting group-by-time data.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: Parallel trends must be stated and supported.

name: DiD: pre-trends shown, null pretest not taken as proof
definition: No pre-period estimates are shown, or parallel trends is concluded from insignificant pre-period coefficients without power or Rambachan-Roth robustness.
divergence: Only jaanch has this; audit-analysis does not mention pretest power.
reason: Pretrends shown; null pretest not proof.

name: DiD: heterogeneity-robust estimator under staggered timing
definition: Staggered adoption is estimated only by TWFE without a cohort-robust estimator (CS, SA, dCDH, BJS) or a Goodman-Bacon weight decomposition.
divergence: jaanch accepts a decomposition OR robust estimator from text; audit-analysis tier4 requires the robust estimator and separately diagnoses contamination by rerun.
reason: TWFE under staggered timing mis-weights effects.

name: DiD: anticipation, reversals, composition changes checked
definition: Anticipation, treatment reversals, changing group composition or outcome-specific trends are not checked.
reason: Anticipation, reversals, composition checked.

name: Panel: dynamics and Nickell bias handled
definition: A short panel with a lagged dependent variable and unit FE uses an inconsistent estimator, or serial correlation and lag structure are unchecked.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: Nickell bias makes dynamic panel estimator inconsistent.

name: Panel: identifying within-unit variation named
definition: The within-unit variation identifying each coefficient is not named, and units with no usable variation are not reported.
reason: Within-unit identifying variation named.

name: RD: genuine assignment rule and running variable verified
definition: The cutoff is not a real assignment rule (analyst-chosen threshold or ranking) or the running variable is constructed differently from the rule.
divergence: assess targets misuse of RD language around analyst cutoffs; audit-analysis verifies a real RD's rule in code.
reason: RD cutoff must be a real assignment rule.

name: RD: no manipulation or covariate jumps at cutoff
definition: Running-variable density or predetermined covariates jump at the cutoff.
reason: Density or covariate jumps at cutoff.

name: AMICUS RD checklist (items unpublished)
definition: Placeholder for AMICUS's 21-item RD checklist; only quoted example is multiple-comparison correction.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: AMICUS RD checklist.

name: Selection on observables: overlap and justified adjustment set
definition: Treated and comparison units lack common support, so regression extrapolates; adjustment variables and conditional comparability are not justified.
reason: Lack of overlap forces extrapolation.

name: Matching/weighting: balance beyond means and weight diagnostics
definition: Balance is shown only on means, weighting diagnostics are missing, or SUTVA is not stated.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: Balance beyond means and weight diagnostics.

name: Mediation: ignorability named and sensitivity reported
definition: A formal mediation analysis omits the no-unmeasured-mediator-outcome-confounding assumption or its sensitivity analysis (Imai-Keele-Tingley).
divergence: Our tools only check informal mechanism claims (identification.mechanism_link_measured).
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: Sequential ignorability named with sensitivity.

name: Structural: what identifies preferences vs beliefs and frictions
definition: Estimated tastes are not separated from beliefs, expected acceptance, strategy, search frictions or restricted choice sets.
reason: Tastes not separated from beliefs and frictions.

name: Discrimination: group coefficient not read as pure prejudice
definition: A social-group coefficient is called pure prejudice though it can carry beliefs about customs or compatibility not removed by controls.
reason: Group coefficient read as prejudice though it carries other constructs.

name: Structural: quantities identified on observed support
definition: Extrapolated WTP or counterfactuals depend on an arbitrary normalization outside the observed support.
reason: Extrapolation outside support rests on arbitrary normalization.

name: Structural: results invariant to observationally equivalent coefficients
definition: A downstream result changes under alternative coefficient vectors that preserve every fitted value of a rank-deficient stage.
reason: Result changes across observationally equivalent coefficients.

name: Structural: estimate bounded over equally-fitting functional forms
definition: The object of interest moves widely across functions in a nesting class that fit at least as well, or bounds are shown without their dependence on the nesting model.
divergence: In-sample only; no sampling uncertainty.
reason: Object of interest moves across equally fitting forms.

name: Discrete choice: choice-based sample and IIA handled
definition: A choice-based sample lacks alternative-specific constants/weights, or nested alternatives are modeled under IIA.
reason: Choice-based sampling and IIA misspecification.

name: AMICUS synthetic-control checklist (items unpublished)
definition: Placeholder for AMICUS's 7-item synthetic-control checklist whose item text is not quoted.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: AMICUS synthetic-control checklist.

name: AMICUS causal-ML checklist (items unpublished)
definition: Placeholder for AMICUS's 10-item causal-ML checklist (excluded from public release).
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: AMICUS causal-ML checklist.

name: ML: baselines, ablations, evaluation settings valid
definition: Invalid baselines, improper ablations or inconsistent evaluation settings across compared systems.
validation: PaperAudit: Qwen3-14B SFT+RL 55.8% F1 at Detection@1 (synthetic errors).
reason: Invalid baselines or ablations break the comparison.

name: Measured construct or unit not swapped for claimed one
definition: The claim is about a construct or unit that was not measured (sales->yield, account->person, sightings->unique people, proxy relabeled as construct).
divergence: Three of our tools state it with different example lists; write-empirical-paper is the author-side version (do not write it), the others reviewer-side.
validation: Dawes construct-validity category: replication relevance HIGH.
reason: Claim names a construct that was not measured.

name: Self-reports and intentions not read as actions
definition: Attitudes, intentions, plans or self-reports stand in for observed actions, or one party's actions are read as another's preferences.
divergence: assess adds decision-maker and choice-set identification.
reason: Self-reports stand in for behavior.

name: Indicator or metric validated for the construct
definition: No validation evidence is cited for indicators of key concepts, or a metric moves without the construct (proxy not checked on known-good/bad changes, novelty decay).
divergence: AMICUS: a citation suffices; empirical-problem-solving demands an empirical test on historical changes. Our paper-review tools (jaanch, audit-analysis) lack a universal 'validation cited' item.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text. Flagged on 67%.
reason: Metric lacks validation for the construct.

name: Measurement error in key variables discussed
definition: Measurement error in key variables is not discussed.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text. Flagged on 64%.
reason: Measurement error in key variables not discussed.

name: 'Conservative due to measurement error' claim justified
definition: A claim that measurement error biases toward zero is made without the (classical, non-differential) error structure that justifies it.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: Attenuation claim lacks the error structure justifying it.

name: Measure equivalent across compared groups or periods
definition: Scores, latent means or paths are compared across groups/waves/contexts, or validation is borrowed, without invariance or comparability evidence.
divergence: jaanch requires the invariance level matching the comparison (scalar for means) from text; audit-analysis tests it on data; AMICUS applies it universally to any cross-context comparison or borrowed validation.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text. Flagged on 86%.
reason: Comparisons need measurement invariance.

name: Reliability reported without overclaiming alpha
definition: Reliability (alpha/omega with uncertainty, interrater, test-retest) is missing for scores analyzed, or alpha is taken as evidence of unidimensionality or validity.
divergence: APA requires reporting; audit-analysis computes and warns alpha rises with item count.
reason: Reliability missing or alpha overread.

name: Reflective vs formative scale treated correctly
definition: A formative/union index is judged by internal consistency, or a composite does not state how its components relate.
divergence: AMICUS measurement checklist has 18 items; only three examples quoted (composites, first-stage handling of estimated scores, convergence diagnostics) and the latter two are absent from our tools.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: Formative index judged by internal consistency.

name: Index rebuilt and claim-literal component checked
definition: An index result is not decomposed; the component closest to the claim does not move, one component drives it, or results depend on weights/thresholds.
divergence: audit-analysis tier4 adds alternative thresholds/weights; assess adds missing-data rules and scaling.
reason: Index result driven by one component or weights.

name: Scale dimensionality checked with suitable factor model
definition: A multi-item scale is assumed unidimensional without a factor model (polychoric for ordinal items).
reason: Dimensionality assumed without factor model.

name: Item-level statistics and drop-one effects reported
definition: Item prevalence, inter-item and item-total correlations and the effect of removing each item are not examined.
reason: Item-level statistics not examined.

name: Reliability and validity types kept distinct
definition: Passing one of reliability, convergent, discriminant, criterion or construct validity is taken as establishing another.
reason: One validity type taken as another.

name: Construct map built and scoring code matches it
definition: Construct, item, scale, coding direction, missingness and aggregation are not traceable, or scoring code mixes opposing items, uses wrong multipliers or silent recodes.
divergence: I4R verifies item mapping against the covariance structure in code; audit-analysis builds the map but does not prescribe that test.
reason: Scoring code does not match construct map.

name: Variable definitions match official codebook
definition: A variable's definition differs from its primary source or official codebook.
reason: Variable definition differs from official codebook.

name: Materials and cell lines correctly identified
definition: Mislabeled materials or known misidentified/contaminated cell lines are used.
validation: SPOT: 3 of 91 real errors in this category.
reason: Misidentified materials mean manipulation is not what claimed.

name: Every ratio's numerator and denominator units explicit
definition: A rate/share/ratio lacks explicit numerator and denominator units, compared quantities do not share both, or a 'rate' is not the ratio its name implies.
divergence: Called the highest-yield check in audit-analysis tier1.
reason: Ratio lacks explicit units or is not what its name says.

name: Ratio outcome decomposed and denominators compared
definition: A ratio change is read as productivity/welfare though driven by the denominator or another component, or by sample composition.
reason: Ratio change driven by denominator, not the named quantity.

name: Control-group level plausible and correctly typed
definition: The comparison mean is implausible against matched benchmarks, or a stock, event rate, cumulative incidence and planned behavior are confused.
reason: Control level implausible or wrongly typed quantity.

name: Floors, ceilings and raw-unit effects inspected
definition: Normalized effects hide floors/ceilings, baseline gaps or mechanically dominant components.
reason: Normalized effects hide floors and ceilings.

name: Zeros, censoring and top-codes distinguished and shown
definition: Measured zero, structural zero, censored and unmeasured values are merged, or displays smooth away zero mass and top-coding.
reason: Zeros, censoring, unmeasured merged.

name: External benchmark matches outcome, population, period, units
definition: A result is supported or refuted by a benchmark with a different outcome, population (adults vs all ages), period, contrast or units.
divergence: write-empirical-paper covers population only; assess covers all five dimensions.
reason: Benchmark measures different outcome, population or period.

name: Population quantities not inferred from selected sample
definition: A population-level share is inferred from a non-representative selected sample.
reason: Population share inferred from selected sample.

name: Constructed categories robust across cutoffs
definition: A binned/thresholded classification yields a result only at one cutoff; continuous measure and classification uncertainty not shown.
reason: Classification result holds only at one cutoff.

name: Omitted reference category is what it is labeled
definition: The omitted group differs across outcome samples or contains units the label excludes.
reason: Reference category is not what it is labeled.

name: Distinct unit roles not merged; denominators bounded
definition: Different unit roles (owners, residents, cultivators) are merged, or an unreported part of a denominator is renormalized away instead of bounded.
reason: Distinct unit roles merged.

name: Replication sample, units, exposure, timing audited
definition: An independent replication uses a sample, unit, exposure definition or timing that does not match the original (e.g. later register as baseline).
reason: Replication uses different units or exposure than original.

name: Geographic aggregation unit substantively defensible
definition: Results are mapped or aggregated at an arbitrary or misleading geographic unit.
reason: Arbitrary geographic unit (MAUP).

name: Panel: FE normalization explained when FE become outcomes
definition: Extracted fixed effects are ranked or transformed without stating the normalization they depend on.
reason: Ranked fixed effects depend on unstated normalization.

name: Structural: WTP ratio constructs and resources specified
definition: A WTP/equivalent-income ratio leaves alternatives, decision maker, income construct or the resource distribution behind the conversion ambiguous.
reason: WTP constructs left ambiguous.

name: Structural: welfare stated in the right unit
definition: Revenue, income, utility, CV and equivalent income are interchanged, or transfers are not separated from resource costs.
reason: Welfare quantities interchanged.

name: Structural: model fit checked on counterfactual-relevant features
definition: Model fit or predictive checks use default or in-sample features unrelated to the counterfactual or scientific question; failures go unreported.
divergence: visualize-evidence phrases it for Bayesian posterior predictive checks; assess for structural counterfactuals.
reason: Model fit checked on irrelevant features.

name: Discrete choice: attributes not proxying alternative category
definition: An attribute built with a category-specific multiplier acts as a category indicator.
reason: Attribute acts as category indicator.

name: Discrete choice: chosen and generated alternatives measured alike
definition: An attribute is measured differently for the chosen alternative than for generated ones, so it predicts choice mechanically.
reason: Chosen alternative measured differently, predicting choice mechanically.

name: ML: label errors hand-audited among failures
definition: Model 'failures' are not hand-audited for label correctness.
validation: Cites >=3.3% label error across ten ML benchmarks.
reason: Labels not audited for correctness.

name: Text-as-data: stability and method checklist
definition: Placeholder for AMICUS's 13-item text-as-data checklist; quoted example: unsupervised models with non-deterministic optimizers report seed/stability handling.
validation: AMICUS (Chau & Little 2026): repeat-coding correlation 0.84 on universal score; 7.4% of flags flip on re-coding identical text.
reason: AMICUS text-as-data method checklist.

name: SEs clustered at unit of independent variation
definition: Standard errors ignore dependence or are clustered at a level other than the one at which treatment/sampling varies independently (too low, or needlessly higher).
divergence: audit-analysis says cluster 'at the unit of variation, and no higher' (Abadie et al. logic); jaanch reasoning only compares cluster unit to treatment unit; assess-empirical-claims frames it as sampling vs assignment vs dependence; design-analysis derives it from assignment+sampling+estimand and runs code. Only design-analysis rejects a universal few-cluster threshold.
reason: Cluster at unit of independent variation.

name: DiD SEs clustered at treatment-varying level
definition: A DiD/event-study reports SEs unclustered or clustered below the level at which treatment varies (serial correlation, Bertrand-Duflo-Mullainathan), or omits the cluster count.
reason: DiD SEs clustered at treatment level.

name: Cluster-randomized trial SEs at assignment level
definition: A group-randomized experiment treats individuals as independent instead of clustering (or analyzing) at the level of assignment; with few clusters per cell, RI or wild bootstrap is not used.
divergence: audit-analysis (Green SOP) adds a ~40-cluster threshold for switching to RI/wild bootstrap; jaanch EXP-INFER-01 has no count threshold.
reason: Cluster-randomized SEs at assignment level.

name: Clusters and treated clusters counted; few-cluster correction
definition: Inference rests on few clusters or few treated clusters (overall or within an exposure-by-status cell), with cluster-size imbalance, but uses standard CRVE without wild-cluster bootstrap/RI.
divergence: Threshold conflict: audit-analysis Green SOP and design-analysis se_ladder.R use FEW_CLUSTERS=40; design-analysis SKILL says assess finite-sample performance 'rather than applying a universal threshold'. assess-empirical-claims uniquely counts clusters per interaction cell.
reason: Few clusters need wild bootstrap or RI.

name: Wild cluster bootstrap specification fully reported
definition: A few-cluster wild bootstrap is run without justified weights/null imposed, or does not report type, cluster variable, draws, seed, tail convention and failed draws.
reason: Wild bootstrap specification fully reported.

name: Wild-cluster and RI p-values not silently swapped
definition: Randomization-inference and wild-cluster p-values (which answer different nulls) are substituted for each other without saying so.
reason: RI and wild p-values answer different nulls.

name: RI permutes the actual assignment mechanism
definition: Randomization inference permutes a regressor that was not randomized, or ignores blocking/clustering of the real assignment, or states no sharp null.
divergence: Duplicate across two of our skills with near-identical wording; design-analysis's se_ladder.R itself 'cannot infer blocked or multilevel assignment', so its RI rung can violate this check.
reason: RI must permute actual assignment.

name: Randomization inference used when assignment is known
definition: When the assignment mechanism is known (an experiment), design-based randomization inference is not reported as the natural test.
reason: Design-based RI expected when assignment known.

name: RI p-value uses (k+1)/(B+1)
definition: A randomization/permutation p-value is computed as k/B, which is anti-conservative and permits p=0.
validation: Bug taxonomy 6a: headline .050 -> .055 when corrected.
reason: Permutation p-value must be (k+1)/(B+1).

name: SE type matches error structure; estimator ladder stable
definition: The variance estimator (iid, HC, CR, CR2, wild, RI) does not match the error structure, and the conclusion flips across defensible estimators (e.g., classical p=.287 vs HC1 p=.001); small-sample HC3 not used where needed.
divergence: design-analysis has a deterministic gate (se_ladder.R exits 1 if the 95% CI crosses zero on some rungs only); audit-analysis does the same by judgment and additionally asks for a heteroskedasticity test/plot and HC3, which se_ladder does not gate.
reason: Variance estimator mismatch flips conclusion.

name: Variance conventions stated, not mixed across columns
definition: SE and finite-sample conventions are undisclosed or silently differ across specifications, columns or package versions.
divergence: audit-analysis se_type_vs_error_structure also asks for consistency but is mapped there; design-analysis se_note() exports the convention.
reason: Variance conventions differ across columns.

name: Clustering/FE not confused with identification or covariance
definition: Clustered SEs are presented as addressing confounding, or fixed effects are presented as a substitute for a correct covariance estimator.
divergence: Two directions of the same confusion; each tool has only one direction.
reason: Clustering or FE confused with identification.

name: Serial/spatial correlation window justified
definition: HAC/Conley-type SEs use an unjustified lag or distance cutoff with no sensitivity reported.
reason: HAC/Conley window unjustified.

name: Collective responses not counted as independent replicates
definition: One collective response (focus group, village meeting) is treated as many independent measurements, inflating N.
reason: Collective response counted as many replicates.

name: Bootstrap resamples every independent level
definition: A bootstrap resamples rows rather than the independent unit, or omits a level of the estimand (needs hierarchical bootstrap).
reason: Bootstrap resamples wrong unit.

name: Failed bootstrap draws counted and reported
definition: A bootstrap SE is built only on converged draws with failures unreported, or too few draws succeeded.
divergence: Gate threshold min_fraction=0.5 is far looser than the prose rule, which wants every failure reported.
reason: Failed bootstrap draws unreported.

name: Degrees of freedom and critical values correct
definition: Inference uses wrong degrees of freedom or critical values, e.g. z instead of t because an estimated variance was treated as known.
reason: Wrong degrees of freedom or critical values.

name: Optimizer converged; estimation problems reported
definition: Estimates from iterative optimizers (GMM, quantile regression, IRLS, ML) were not verified at the optimum or convergence problems/software were not reported.
validation: Bug taxonomy 6e: IRLS quantile regression ~1% off.
reason: Optimizer convergence not verified.

name: Residual diagnostics tied to an assumption
definition: Residual diagnostics are reported as ritual without stating which assumption each probes and how it changes inference.
reason: Residual diagnostics not tied to assumptions.

name: Design matrix rank, conditioning, VIF, effective n
definition: Rank, condition number, VIF, leverage and effective sample size of the design matrix are not examined, hiding near-collinearity.
reason: Design matrix collinearity unexamined.

name: Requested contrasts estimable; dropped terms not zero
definition: A contrast is not estimable, or a collinearity-dropped coefficient is read as a zero effect.
reason: Inestimable contrast or dropped term read as zero.

name: Joint test not read as coefficient-specific
definition: A joint-null test (e.g., joint AR) is presented as evidence about one coefficient or interaction.
reason: Joint test read as coefficient-specific evidence.

name: Non-significance not read as no effect
definition: A non-significant estimate (or a hypothesis 'crossed off' by a weak test) is read as no/negligible effect without an interval in substantive units or an equivalence bound excluding consequential effects.
divergence: Evidence bar differs: jaanch passes on any equivalence test/bound/CI support (if_silent pass) and duplicates itself in two finders; audit-analysis requires the interval in substantive units plus the largest effect it permits; assess-empirical-claims requires a predefined equivalence range for 'negligible' claims. None of ours uses metacheck's deterministic p>.05 sentence extractor as a candidate generator.
validation: metacheck p>.05 detector: 1,783 ground-truth p-values in 749 papers, 3.6% missed, 94.8% precision (detection only). AMICUS: flagged in 70% of papers.
reason: Null read as no effect.

name: Differences tested directly, not via significance labels
definition: A claim that effects differ (groups, waves, doses, slopes) rests on one being significant and the other not, or a figure invites overlapping-CI comparison, instead of a direct test of the difference/interaction.
divergence: audit-analysis and assess-empirical-claims both note it is recomputable from reported estimates and SEs (z = diff/sqrt(se1^2+se2^2) under an assumed covariance) but no script exists; jaanch treats it as pure judgment. Nyhan adds marginal-effect interpretation of interactions (Brambor-Clark-Golder) which none of ours states.
reason: Differences must be tested directly.

name: Statistical significance not equated with importance
definition: Statistical significance is described as practical or substantive importance.
reason: Significance equated with importance.

name: 'Marginally significant' language flagged
definition: Results with p above the threshold are described as marginally significant or trending.
validation: metacheck: 51 papers, 87 statements; PPV 63%, missed 42%.
reason: 'Marginally significant' language overstates evidence.

name: Multiple comparisons corrected or primary designated
definition: Conclusions rest on a family of related tests (outcomes, subgroups, moderators) with no correction (Bonferroni/Holm/BH) and no pre-specified primary test.
divergence: jaanch accepts either correction or a designated primary; audit-analysis move 8 applies the correction itself over the declared family.
reason: Multiple comparisons uncorrected.

name: Multiplicity family defined and matches reported statistic
definition: The multiplicity family is undefined, chosen post hoc to rescue/kill significance, or does not match the statistic reported (e.g., Bonferroni over levels while claims are about changes).
validation: Bug taxonomy 6c.
reason: Multiplicity family undefined or mismatched.

name: Many related estimates pooled, not independent tests
definition: Many related subgroup/unit estimates are treated as independent tests rather than partially pooled (or at least declared as a family).
reason: Related estimates not partially pooled.

name: Slice scans report denominator and FDR q-values
definition: A striking slice is reported without the number of slices scanned or without FDR-adjusted q-values and a minimum support.
validation: scripts/test_slice_discipline.py: 20,000 rows, 15 dims, no cause; naive scan fires 97% of runs, discipline 0%; both find a planted cause 100%.
reason: Slice scans need denominator and FDR.

name: Planned vs exploratory analyses labeled
definition: Subgroup, dose or other secondary analyses added after the fact are presented as confirmatory rather than labeled exploratory, or lack theoretical motivation/power.
divergence: Nyhan also requires subgroups to be adequately powered; our design-analysis row requires only labeling.
reason: Exploratory analyses presented as confirmatory.

name: Analytic flexibility: choices made after seeing data
definition: Outcome coding, exclusions, covariates, subgroups or thresholds have unconstrained degrees of freedom (many DVs without a primary, vague exclusions, unjustified covariates) and no preregistration or defensible-set report.
reason: Unconstrained analytic flexibility.

name: Hypotheses confirmed on held-out data
definition: A hypothesis or fix is found and confirmed on the same data, the holdout was touched during development, or the in-sample gain far exceeds the out-of-sample gain.
validation: Part of the simulated slice discipline (see slice_scan_denominator_fdr).
reason: Hypothesis confirmed on same data.

name: Improvement on worst slice measured on fresh draw
definition: A unit/slice selected for being worst is re-measured on the same draw, scoring regression to the mean as improvement.
reason: Regression to the mean scored as improvement.

name: Sample size and power justified
definition: Author-collected data have no stated reason for the sample size (power/precision analysis or resource constraint), or the metric cannot detect the expected effect at the available n/horizon.
divergence: jaanch restricts to author-collected data; CONSORT/APA add interim analyses and stopping rules, which none of ours checks.
reason: Sample size and power unjustified.

name: Retrospective power, Type S and Type M error
definition: Given the design SE and an externally plausible effect, the design is so underpowered that a significant estimate is likely exaggerated (Type M) or wrong-signed (Type S).
divergence: Both are model-run although retrodesign (R) exists; the plausible-effect input needs a literature lookup that neither tool specifies.
reason: Type S/M error from design SE.

name: Coverage simulated when nominal intervals doubtful
definition: Nominal intervals are trusted in small samples or under strained assumptions without simulating coverage.
reason: Interval coverage not simulated when doubtful.

name: Estimate located in its defensible specification family
definition: Robustness is claimed from one alternative, or only favorable (or only breaking) choices are reported, instead of the range of estimates/intervals across a reasoned set of sample, estimand, adjustment and dependence choices.
divergence: audit-analysis's gate demands the published estimate be the smallest-magnitude member of the family (a conservatism gate); assess-empirical-claims only asks that preserving choices be shown too; I4R requires robustness checks pre-specified after coding errors are fixed, which none of ours requires. audit-analysis alone separates estimand-changing from estimate-only forks.
reason: Estimate not located in specification family.

name: Estimate shown across every natural split
definition: One pooled number is reported where the estimate could be shown with intervals across subsets, waves or specifications (the 'secret weapon').
reason: Estimate not shown across natural splits.

name: Result not carried by one unit or cluster
definition: The headline moves materially when one observation, cluster, subgroup or specification is dropped (DFBETA/leave-one-out/leave-one-cluster-out).
divergence: audit_data.leverage flags any coefficient moved >= 0.5 SE by one row, OLS only and row-level not cluster-level; the prose rules ask for leave-one-cluster-out and the full range of p-values, which the script does not compute.
validation: Closed-form LOO verified identical to refit loop to 8 decimals.
reason: Result carried by one unit or cluster.

name: Ratio outcomes: tiny denominators and precision weighting
definition: Ratio outcomes resting on very few observations drive results, or are equally weighted despite widely varying precision.
validation: Example: 13 units <10 obs, 77 <100; dropping raised 2.809 to 3.010.
reason: Tiny denominators drive ratio outcomes.

name: Heavy-tailed outcomes use resampling inference
definition: Asymptotic inference is used on heavy-tailed data without bootstrap/permutation or leverage checks.
reason: Heavy tails need resampling inference.

name: Back-transformed log means corrected for retransformation
definition: Means back-transformed from log/asinh outcomes ignore E[log Y] != log E[Y] (no smearing).
reason: Retransformation bias uncorrected.

name: Generated regressors' estimation uncertainty propagated
definition: Fitted FEs, residuals, propensity scores, imputed values, embeddings or ML predictions used downstream are treated as known, with no analytic correction, joint estimation, sample splitting or full-pipeline bootstrap.
reason: Generated regressor uncertainty ignored.

name: Ratio estimands carry numerator and denominator uncertainty
definition: A ratio of estimates (WTP, Wald ITT/first stage) is reported without propagating numerator, denominator and preliminary-stage uncertainty, or with a near-zero denominator.
reason: Ratio estimand uncertainty not propagated.

name: WTP and WTP gaps get proper intervals
definition: Percentile rows of a mixed-logit WTP distribution are presented as an interval for the mean, or WTP/group gaps lack a delta-method/bootstrap interval.
validation: Bug taxonomy 8b.
reason: WTP percentile rows misused as intervals.

name: Mixed logit fit gain over conditional logit
definition: Mixed-logit heterogeneity is claimed when the log-likelihood barely improves on conditional logit, i.e. heterogeneity is imposed by the mixing family.
validation: Bug taxonomy 8d (-7,985 vs -7,986).
reason: Log-likelihood gain too small to support heterogeneity.

name: Uncertainty propagated through full structural procedure
definition: Structural intervals reflect only the last estimation stage, not preliminary estimates, preferences, market composition, matching, simulation.
reason: Structural uncertainty only from last stage.

name: Inclusion probabilities consistent with sampling design
definition: Sampling weights violate sum(pi)=n for a fixed-size design, or pi=min(n*p,1) is used for successive sampling where pi must be simulated under the design that ran.
validation: Bug taxonomy 6b: sum 91.10 for n=100; estimate 8.45 -> 8.11.
reason: Inclusion probabilities inconsistent with sampling design.

name: Event-study simultaneous bands; pretrend test power
definition: Event-time estimates are shown with pointwise bands only, or a null pretrend test is taken as establishing parallel trends without reporting its power and the violations it cannot reject.
divergence: Overlaps jaanch DID-IDENT-02 (identification category, not in this file).
reason: Event-study bands pointwise; pretest power unreported.

name: Weak-IV robust inference, first stage, reduced form
definition: IV inference relies on Wald/bootstrap intervals with a weak first stage instead of AR-type robust inference, or omits the first stage in units, the reduced form and the implied scaling.
divergence: audit-analysis is a reporting check from tables; assess-empirical-claims reruns AR.
reason: Weak-IV robust inference missing.

name: Correct excluded-instrument strength statistic
definition: Instrument strength is reported with the overall first-stage F or an ordinary clustered F instead of the excluded-instrument robust/effective F.
reason: Wrong instrument-strength statistic.

name: IV diagnostics match instrument/regressor count
definition: Single-endogenous diagnostics (separate first-stage Fs, tF) are applied to a model with several endogenous regressors or instruments.
reason: IV diagnostics mismatch model dimension.

name: IV bootstrap resamples clusters and all stages
definition: IV bootstrap ignores clusters, reuses IDs for repeated clusters, skips preliminary stages, hides failures, or is presented as weak-IV-robust.
reason: IV bootstrap ignores clusters or stages.

name: First stage not driven by few clusters
definition: The first stage's variation comes from a few influential observations or clusters.
reason: First stage driven by few clusters.

name: RD bias-corrected inference and bandwidth sensitivity
definition: RD inference is conventional rather than robust bias-corrected, or results are not shown across bandwidth, polynomial order, kernel, donut and discrete-score choices.
reason: RD inference not robust or bandwidth-sensitive.

name: Balance via raw differences and equivalence bounds
definition: Balance is declared because covariate p-values exceed .05 or from an omnibus test, rather than raw differences, intervals, overlap and meaningful equivalence bounds.
reason: Balance judged by p-values misstates randomization's success.

name: Nuisance models cross-fit or sample-split
definition: Causal-ML nuisance functions (DML etc.) are fit and evaluated on the same sample without honest splitting or cross-fitting.
reason: Nuisance models not cross-fit.

name: ML calibration, tuning leakage, repeated search
definition: Prediction/causal-ML results suffer tuning leakage, poor calibration, thin subgroup support or repeated analyst search.
reason: Tuning leakage and calibration problems.

name: Prediction and evaluation target share noise
definition: The same runs/observations enter both a prediction and its evaluation target, inducing covariance that inflates apparent accuracy relative to independent repetitions.
validation: Posthoc Gaussian null: final seed vs 3-seed target containing it 69.6% sign agreement vs 50% independent. Proposed, not in production.
reason: Shared noise inflates accuracy.

name: Ablations replicated across seeds and tuning budgets
definition: An ablation is called causal with one seed and one tuning budget per arm.
reason: Single-seed ablation called causal.

name: Heterogeneous effects reported as policy summaries with uncertainty
definition: HTE results report the most extreme leaves/groups rather than policy-relevant summaries with uncertainty, or skip the method-specific HTE checklist (unconfoundedness, subgroup multiplicity).
divergence: AMICUS has a 12-item HTE checklist; ours has one item.
reason: HTE extremes reported instead of policy summaries.

name: Multilevel model checklist
definition: A multilevel model fails one of AMICUS's six method-specific multilevel checks (item text not public).
reason: AMICUS multilevel model checklist.

name: Probability/dependence statements reconstructed and checked
definition: An asserted unbiasedness, independence or variance identity fails once random variables, conditioning, assignment/sampling units and order of limits are written out.
divergence: Proposed only; not in production jaanch prompts.
reason: Probability identity fails when written out; proof logic.

name: Derived theoretical quantity has an estimation route
definition: A paper derives a theoretical quantity with no discussion of how to estimate it (rates, feasibility, dimensionality).
reason: Derived quantity lacks estimation route; limits usefulness.

name: Intervals only where the design supports them
definition: An interval is drawn on a cell the design cannot support (one cluster) or on a census/deterministic total with no defined source of uncertainty.
reason: Interval drawn where design supports no uncertainty.

name: Transform every posterior/simulation draw before summarizing
definition: A nonlinear substantive quantity is computed from a point estimate with a symmetric SE rather than per draw.
reason: Nonlinear quantity not computed per draw.

name: Posterior distribution shown when shape matters
definition: A point-and-interval summary hides skew, multimodality, bounds, tail risk or dependence that matters.
reason: Interval summary hides posterior shape.

name: MCMC convergence diagnostics inspected
definition: Posterior summaries are interpreted without trace, rank, autocorrelation or convergence diagnostics.
reason: MCMC diagnostics not inspected.

name: Prior sensitivity shown
definition: Prior-driven results are presented as data-driven without comparing prior, likelihood and posterior.
reason: Prior sensitivity not shown.

name: p-value distribution shows evidential value, not selection
definition: Across a set of tests/studies, the significant p- or z-values are not right-skewed (p-curve), are flatter than 33% power, or the expected discovery rate falls well below the observed rate (z-curve).
reason: p-curve/z-curve on reported test statistics.

name: Results too clean to be honest (excess success)
definition: A paper's results are improbably clean: all predictions confirmed, no nulls, interactions without main effects, or insufficient variance in test statistics (TIVA/R-Index).
reason: Improbably clean results suggest selective reporting.

name: Statistical tests appropriate and fully described
definition: Statistical methods for primary, subgroup and adjusted analyses (incl. missing data) are not described, or tests/statistics are misused or inappropriate for the data.
validation: SPOT: 4 of 91 confirmed errata errors; best model recall 21.1%, precision 6.1% overall. FLAWS: best GPT-5 39.1% identification at k=10 overall.
reason: Tests inappropriate or undescribed.

name: Every outcome reported with effect size and precision
definition: Outcomes lack per-group effect sizes with CIs, absolute and relative effects for binary outcomes, or unadjusted alongside adjusted estimates.
reason: Required effect sizes and CIs per outcome missing.

name: Sampling supports the generalization claimed
definition: Sampling procedure is not valid or stable enough for the population the inference generalizes to.
reason: Sampling does not support the population generalized to.

name: Derivation step wrong: sign, factor, index, dropped term
definition: A step of an equation or derivation does not follow: wrong sign, missing factor, index or subscript slip, inconsistent units/powers of n, or a term dropped from an expanded identity without justification.
divergence: Production jaanch_check_reasoning says redo each step 'mechanically with Python/sympy where possible' but ships no script; the two experimental refinements (expand the full identity before applying assumptions; oracle-policy negative control and unit/power-of-n check) exist only in eval/flaws/strategies.md, each observed on one dev case and not promoted.
validation: SPOT: real erratum errors, 37 of 91 are equation/proof; best model (o3) recall 21.1%, precision 6.1%. ReviewerGPT: GPT-4 found 7/13 inserted errors (math+conceptual). FLAWS: best GPT-5 39.1% identification at k=10 across all types. PaperAudit-Bench: Qwen3-14B SFT+RL 55.8% F1 Detection@1 (all types). jaanch-experimental expand-identity: found the omitted cross term on dev case 01 only.
reason: Derivation step wrong.

name: Invoked theorem or lemma used outside its hypotheses
definition: A proof applies a named theorem or lemma (or relies on an assumption) whose conditions are neither stated nor shown to hold here, e.g. a concentration bound needing bounded data applied to finite-variance data, or a width guarantee used as a residual guarantee without a regularity condition.
divergence: jaanch runs this twice: as checklist item PRF-DERIV-01 in jaanch_check_completeness (omission framing, if_silent=flag) and as a reasoning-finder bullet 'is every assumption used actually stated' (error framing). The experimental dependency map (result -> lemma -> assumption) is the only version that enumerates candidates systematically; the production versions rely on the reader noticing.
validation: FLAWS 'Error in assumptions' is the largest post hoc label (Gemini 257 / GPT-5 104 inserted errors); labels assigned after insertion, not a design taxonomy.
reason: Theorem applied outside its hypotheses.

name: Proof misses a case, boundary or degenerate input
definition: A proof by cases or by strict inequality omits a case not excluded by assumption: equality, zero, negative, corner or degenerate input.
divergence: Exact duplicate inside jaanch: PRF-DERIV-02 (completeness finder, if_silent=pass) and the reasoning finder proofs bullet. coarse enumerates per assumption ('for each assumption, are boundary cases handled'), which is a better candidate generator than either jaanch wording.
validation: Refine (Dawes benchmark, all categories): 57/100 planted errors caught from ~305 findings; not category-specific for proofs.
reason: Proof misses a case.

name: Quantifiers, domain or limiting regime differ from claim
definition: The proof's quantifiers or their order, parameter domain, probability law or limiting regime do not match the claim, e.g. pointwise convergence offered for a uniform guarantee, or a local result extended to trajectories or warm starts without argument.
divergence: Production asks only 'do the quantifiers and their order match'; experimental guarantee_domain_audit widens scope to parameter domain, probability law, limiting regime and every factor of a composed operator (e.g. fixing G in K=DGD^T does not fix K when D changes). Experimental notes warn a finite witness must not refute a correctly restricted asymptotic theorem; production has no such guard.
validation: pointwise_vs_uniform observed on dev case 03; guarantee_domain_audit proposed after p08 (all systems found the target by some route); no transfer measurement.
reason: Quantifiers or domain mismatch the claim.

name: Conditioning, timing or stopping rule misused
definition: A conditional-expectation identity or rate argument fails because what is chosen before vs after an observation, clock time vs sample count, or phase-end vs required lower bounds are conflated.
divergence: Only in jaanch-experimental; production reasoning finder mentions 'conditioning' in the derivation bullet but gives no timeline procedure.
validation: sampling_decision_timeline: dev case 03, both configurations found the planted defect at rank 1. clock_time_vs_sample_count: dev case 01 only.
reason: Conditioning or timing misused in proof.

name: Result proved is weaker than result claimed
definition: The argument establishes a weaker statement than the theorem or discussion claims: necessity read as sufficiency, testable restriction read as identification, special case read as general, a local approximation stated as an exact equality, or an inequality of the wrong direction/strength.
divergence: jaanch checks proof vs theorem statement only; coarse also checks the discussion against the formal results (cross-section pass), which jaanch splits off into the per-section conclusion bullet. jaanch-experimental adds a false-positive guard: weakening an upper bound does not itself invalidate it.
reason: Proves weaker than claimed.

name: Claimed invariance not preserved through later operations
definition: A claimed symmetry or invariance holds for one component but is broken by normalization, residual addition or a later operator in the full computation.
validation: Observed success on p06 across all discovery branches; transfer untested.
reason: Claimed invariance broken later.

name: Stated relation fails on an admissible counterexample
definition: A central claim, once formalized (estimand, assumptions, quantifiers, implication), fails on a small admissible instance or a stable seeded simulation that satisfies every stated assumption.
divergence: All six are candidate mechanisms for the same failure, none in production. They differ on the evidence bar: numerical_falsification requires an analytical explanation after the simulation; witness_search requires exact arithmetic and records unresolved outcomes; formalize_central_claim requires a precise missing implication. Shared guard: a zero-finding bounded search is not proof.
validation: formalize addendum: 1 of 2 targets vs 2 of 2 for incumbent, dev gate failed. independent passes: 2 of 2 vs 1 for baseline on two dev papers, not selected by tie-break. relation_audit: in frozen 16-paper comparison each judge found 13 material groups in relation reports absent from repeated review, repeated review kept 3-4 absent from relation; missed p07 shared-noise issue; no target gain.
reason: Admissible counterexample computed by simulation.

name: Algorithm as written does not produce claimed target
definition: Executing the paper's literal update rule or procedure on a minimal admissible model (exact arithmetic) gives a result that disagrees with an independently computed target.
validation: Observed on dev case 02 (clipping rule, zero confidence bonus, backward induction contradicting a stage-invariant value).
reason: Literal procedure executed disagrees with target.

name: Main formal result not shown to have bite
definition: The paper never shows its main result is non-vacuous: no DGP that violates a testable restriction, no worked identification example, no simulation for a proposed estimator.
reason: Main result never shown to have bite.

name: Conclusion stronger than the evidence shown
definition: A stated conclusion or interpretation does not follow from what the paper shows, or leans silently on another unproven claim (e.g. low power read as a small true effect).
divergence: jaanch runs it per section ('follows from what the section shows'), so cross-section overclaims (abstract vs results) fall between finders; audit-analysis Q4 frames it as 'what does the result not establish' and requires naming the silently-leaned-on claim; write-referee-report has no checklist ('underspecified'). None of ours defines an evidence bar beyond judgment.
validation: King & Worthington: GPT-5.5 judge flagged 5.5% of AI review claims vs 15.9% of human claims as incorrect; caught 258/258 planted false sentences, 0/258 false alarms (judge validation, not detection). Stanford: Spearman AI-human 0.42 (score, not finding). Reviewer3 Dawes 30/100 overall.
reason: Conclusion stronger than evidence.

name: Abstract or introduction promises what paper never delivers
definition: Implications or contributions promised in the abstract or introduction are not developed in the body.
reason: Abstract promises not delivered in body.

name: Causal or mechanistic language for descriptive/predictive evidence
definition: A claim is phrased as causal, mechanistic or extrapolative when the design supports only description or prediction (including predictive ML performance presented as causal identification).
divergence: assess-empirical-claims uses four classes (description, causal, mechanism, extrapolation); audit-analysis uses three (descriptive, predictive, causal) and feeds verdict labels. Neither has a candidate generator; metacheck runs a deterministic classifier (causal_relation_miner) over title and abstract to list candidate causal sentences but does not judge warrant.
validation: metacheck module validated mostly on Psychological Science papers (per-module <validation> tags).
reason: Causal language for descriptive evidence.

name: Mechanism asserted without measured evidence
definition: An asserted mechanism is stated as a finding without measured awareness, exposure, take-up or mediation; plausibility alone is offered.
divergence: audit-analysis requires measured evidence (strict); write-empirical-paper accepts relabeling the mechanism as a hypothesis (author-side remedy).
reason: Mechanism asserted without evidence.

name: Explanation relies on factor shared by both groups
definition: A treatment-control difference is attributed to a cost or factor that does not differ between groups.
reason: Explanation relies on factor not differing by group.

name: Rival mechanism predicting same pattern not ruled out
definition: A rival explanation predicts the same pattern and is not separated by the evidence, yet one cause is named; the search stopped at the first sufficient explanation.
divergence: empirical-problem-solving sets the reporting bar (report the surviving set and the test that splits it); audit-analysis only asks to search for a rival.
reason: Rival explanation predicting same pattern not ruled out.

name: Direction of proposed or induced bias misstated
definition: A proposed bias (confounding, exclusion, measurement, imputation fill) would push the estimate the other way from what the argument needs, or its direction and magnitude are not stated.
divergence: assess-empirical-claims checks critics' bias stories; audit-analysis checks the analyst's own fills (one-sentence direction rule); STROBE asks authors for direction and magnitude.
validation: audit-analysis rejected-finding example: 'structural zeros inflate the age gap' had the sign backwards.
reason: Bias direction misstated.

name: Scope of conclusion exceeds sites, sample or local effect
definition: The title or conclusion generalizes beyond the sites, period, selected sample or local estimand (e.g. RD effect extrapolated from the cutoff), or unacknowledged breakdown conditions exist.
divergence: audit-analysis lays sample context beside title breadth; assess-empirical-claims also separates local vs average effects and fitted counterfactuals vs observed welfare; rd_no_extrapolation is the RD special case.
validation: Dawes: Refine caught 3/10 generalizability errors.
reason: Conclusion generalizes beyond sites, sample or local estimand.

name: Control or comparison mean implies implausible behavior
definition: A control or comparison-group level, read literally as a standalone claim, implies behavior or institutional arrangements inconsistent with rules, administrative records or matched primary studies.
reason: Control level inconsistent with administrative records.

name: Effect size implausible against bounds and primary studies
definition: The magnitude (or implied exchange rate such as value of time vs wage) exceeds physical bounds, baseline risk, or primary studies of comparable intensity, or a large persistent gain lacks an account of why entry, bargaining or substitution did not erode it.
divergence: audit-analysis states the same check four times (move 7, adversarial bounds, literature 'strongest benchmark', output table) with no single threshold; its table format (number, implied quantity, benchmark, violated expectation, status) is the only evidence bar. assess-empirical-claims probes economic responses instead of external numbers.
reason: Effect magnitude implausible against primary studies.

name: Hypothetical scenario or parity benchmark presented as fact
definition: A hypothetical scenario, parity benchmark or assumed price/quantity is presented as an observed quantity, established norm or statistical null.
reason: Hypothetical presented as observed.

name: Non-independent or external evidence passed off as identified
definition: Corroborating evidence uses the same sample/interview or an in-sample index yet is called independent validation, or external/companion evidence is merged with what the study itself identifies.
divergence: audit-analysis move 10 is a search step (read companion papers for supporting or contradicting facts); assess-empirical-claims judges independence of evidence already cited.
reason: Non-independent evidence called validation.

name: Narrative follows significance stars or post hoc framing
definition: The narrative rests on a subset of estimates (significant vs insignificant coefficient instead of a direct contrast), omits support/nonsupport for some hypotheses, or uses results-dependent (HARKing) framing.
divergence: audit-analysis asks a counterfactual ('what would have been emphasized had the sign changed'); assess-empirical-claims compares against all estimates; neither looks for HARKing language, which Dawes rates CRITICAL.
reason: Narrative follows stars or HARKing.

name: Estimand fork treated as a correction or pooled
definition: An alternative number that targets a different estimand (weighted vs unweighted, mean vs median) is presented as a correction of the same estimand, or estimand forks are pooled into one curve, range or significant-cell count.
divergence: design-analysis applies it pre-analysis (list forks, label each, state supporting/weakening numbers); audit-analysis applies it post hoc to reported results.
reason: Different estimand presented as correction.

name: Defensible analytic choice called an error in a correction
definition: In a correction or audit, a defensible choice is labeled an error without establishing why it is wrong here, a method revision is folded into a coding correction, interacting fixes are given an additive decomposition, or the account of changes over- or under-states which claims survive.
divergence: Only corrigendum; not applied by audit-analysis or jaanch when they report findings.
reason: Defensible choice called an error in a correction.

name: Quantity and question not statable plainly
definition: The quantity computed and the question it answers cannot be stated plainly in one or two sentences, or key terms are insufficiently or inconsistently defined.
reason: Quantity and question cannot be stated plainly.

name: Theory, framework or term misapplied to the question
definition: The theoretical framework or terminology is misused, misapplied or ill-suited to the research question and findings.
reason: Theory or term misapplied.

name: Procedure yields same evidence whether hypothesis true or false
definition: A check or procedure has no result that would refute the hypothesis, e.g. it inspects only failures without the base rate among successes, or would produce the same output under the null.
reason: Procedure cannot refute hypothesis.

name: Stated limitation caused by extraction, not the world
definition: A stated limitation (data unavailable, small n, missing variable) reflects which file was read rather than the phenomenon.
reason: Reviewer-stated limitation reflects files read, not paper.

name: Coefficient, fixed effect or bound misinterpreted
definition: A log, interaction, standardized coefficient, unit fixed effect (read as a trait without shrinkage) or sensitivity interval (read as robustness on a non-exact or capped side) is interpreted incorrectly.
reason: Estimate misinterpreted.

name: Willingness, attribute change and welfare conflated
definition: Willingness to sacrifice is equated with realized sacrifice, or average partner-attribute changes or counts of reallocations are read as welfare.
reason: Willingness, attribute change and welfare conflated.

name: Illustration or partial result presented as evidence
definition: A simulation or worked example is presented as evidence on observed truth, or a partial result as a usable method.
reason: Illustration presented as evidence.

name: Individual and group-level relationships differ in sign
definition: The relationship reverses between individual and group level (Simpson's paradox) and the paper does not say which question it asks.
reason: Individual and group relationships reverse sign.

name: Result depends on unjustified functional form or thin support
definition: A dose or continuous-exposure result depends on a functional form not justified by the design or on thin support.
reason: Dose result depends on unjustified functional form.

name: Mapped hot spot driven by size, area or pooling
definition: A mapped pattern is narrated though sample size, area, density, coverage or partial pooling could create it, with no support/uncertainty or nonspatial companion display.
reason: Map hot spot artifact of size or pooling.

name: Novelty or credit claim anticipated by prior work
definition: A claim of novelty or credit ('we are the first', 'unlike prior work', listed contributions) is undercut by published work answering the same question, using the same method, or obtaining the result.
divergence: jaanch enumerates explicit novelty phrases and searches Scholar/OpenAlex/arXiv/SSRN/NBER/RePEc with a precision bar ('three works that undercut a claim beat twenty merely related'); write-referee-report says only 'compare with the closest primary literature' with no search procedure.
validation: Stanford: originality is a score (Spearman AI-human 0.42 overall), not a finding.
reason: Novelty claim undercut by prior work.

name: Claimed generalization never shown to recover original
definition: A result claimed to generalize an existing result is never verified to recover the original as a special case.
reason: Generalization never shown to recover original.

name: Importance and value of contribution not assessed
definition: The importance of the question and value of the contribution are not judged separately from correctness and originality.
validation: Stanford: acceptance AUC 0.75 (human 0.84) for the combined score.
reason: Reviewer must judge importance separately.

name: Alternative data, theory or literature not offered
definition: The review does not identify alternative data, theory or literature that would strengthen the paper.
reason: Reviewer suggests alternative data or literature.

name: Data availability statement present
definition: The paper never says whether or where the data can be accessed.
divergence: No tool of ours checks this. metacheck open_practices also covers code/materials/registration in one module; CONSORT 2025 item 4 bundles data + code + materials for trials.
validation: ODDPub sens 0.73 / spec 0.97 (Riedel 2020, 792 pubs); rtransparent sens 76% / spec >98% (Serghiou 2021, 6,017 PMC); metacheck open_practices lower FN, higher FP than ODDPub (no numbers).
reason: Data availability statement required.

name: Code availability statement present
definition: The paper never says whether or where the analysis code can be accessed.
divergence: No tool of ours checks this.
validation: ODDPub sens 0.73 / spec ~0.99 (11 positives); rtransparent sens 59% / spec >98%.
reason: Code availability statement required.

name: Questionnaire and materials needed to replicate provided
definition: The instrument, stimuli or materials needed to rerun the study are not provided.
reason: Instruments and materials required.

name: Research resources uniquely identified (RRIDs)
definition: Antibodies, cell lines, organisms or software are named without a unique identifier.
validation: No accuracy published (proprietary).
reason: RRIDs required.

name: Conflict-of-interest statement present
definition: The paper has no statement of authors' financial or other conflicts of interest.
divergence: No tool of ours. CONSORT 2025 row also requires patient/public involvement (item 8), which no script detects.
validation: rtransparent sens >95% / spec >98%; metacheck reuses rtransparent code.
reason: COI statement required.

name: Funding source and funder role stated
definition: The paper does not state its funding sources (and, per STROBE/CONSORT, the funder's role).
divergence: Scripts detect presence only; STROBE/CONSORT also require funder role. APA author-note item also bundles registration, prior use of data and conflicts.
validation: rtransparent sens >95% / spec >98%.
reason: Funding statement required.

name: Preregistration or protocol registration stated
definition: The paper does not say whether the study was registered, or gives no registry/identifier.
divergence: Generic presence check; see reporting.trial_registry_protocol_sap for the trial-specific version.
validation: rtransparent sens >95% / spec >98%.
reason: Registration statement required.

name: Trial registry, protocol and analysis plan locatable
definition: A randomized trial omits registry name/number (AEA: in title footnote), protocol access or SAP access.
divergence: CONSORT 2025 adds SAP access and registry date; AEA requires a specific location (title footnote). CONSORT 2010 row also bundles funding.
reason: Trial registry, protocol, SAP required.

name: Ethics/IRB approval or exemption stated
definition: Data on people (or animals) are used with no statement of IRB/ethics approval or exemption.
divergence: SciScore includes IACUC (animals); AEA asks only when human data plausibly required it.
reason: Ethics approval statement required.

name: Replication README covers required elements
definition: README lacks data availability/provenance, dataset list, compute requirements, code description, instructions or table-to-program map.
reason: README required elements.

name: Deposit has no ZIPs, duplicates, empty files
definition: The replication deposit contains ZIP archives, duplicate or zero-byte files, oversized files or bad metadata.
reason: Deposit hygiene rules.

name: Every data column documented in codebook
definition: Data columns lack a codebook/README definition, or documented variables do not exist in the data.
validation: Not validated.
reason: Data columns compared with codebook.

name: Dataset repository follows Psych-DS standard
definition: The data repository is missing required files or misplaces files relative to Psych-DS.
divergence: Field-specific (psychology) standard.
reason: Psych-DS structure rules.

name: Analytic N and every exclusion counted
definition: The final analytic N is missing, or units drop between stages without a stated count and reason.
divergence: Only jaanch; consistency of N across exhibits is a separate consistency check.
reason: Analytic N and exclusions required.

name: Eligibility criteria, sampling method, participation rate stated
definition: Inclusion/exclusion criteria, sampling method, participation rate, setting or dates are not reported.
divergence: No tool of ours; jaanch sample_flow counts exclusions but does not require criteria or participation rate.
validation: SciScore: none published.
reason: Eligibility, sampling, participation needed to judge generalization.

name: Observational setting, dates and selection methods described
definition: A cohort/case-control/cross-sectional study omits setting, dates, eligibility or case/control selection and matching.
reason: Setting and selection methods required for observational studies.

name: Observational design named in title or abstract
definition: The title/abstract does not name the observational design with a common term.
divergence: Parallel to reporting.trial_identified_in_title (CONSORT 1a).
reason: Design named in title or abstract.

name: Randomized trial identified in title; structured abstract
definition: A randomized trial is not identified as such in the title, or the abstract is not structured.
reason: Trial identified in title; structured abstract.

name: Objectives and prespecified hypotheses stated
definition: Hypotheses (primary vs secondary) and how the design tests them are not stated.
divergence: No tool of ours asks for this directly; APA additionally requires primary/secondary separation.
reason: Hypotheses and objectives required.

name: Post-commencement trial design changes reported
definition: Design, allocation ratio, or changes to methods after the trial began (with reasons) are not reported.
divergence: Generic analogue is reporting.deviations_from_plan.
reason: Post-commencement design changes required.

name: Treatment and context described enough to replicate
definition: The intervention and its context are not described well enough to replicate or judge external/construct validity.
divergence: No tool of ours. I4R applies to any treatment evaluation, not only RCTs.
reason: Intervention detail needed to judge treatment construct.

name: Randomization unit, method and stratification described
definition: An experiment says units were randomized but not what, at what level, or how (blocking/stratification/cluster).
divergence: metacheck/SciScore detect any randomization sentence (presence); jaanch requires unit, method and blocking (completeness).
reason: Randomization unit and method required.

name: Blinding of investigators or assessors reported
definition: The paper does not say whether investigators/outcome assessors were blinded.
reason: Blinding status required.

name: Baseline characteristics reported by arm
definition: An experiment with pre-treatment covariates gives no baseline table by arm (or recruitment dates / stop reason).
divergence: jaanch explicitly does not require balance tests (Mutz et al.); CONSORT also asks recruitment dates and why trial ended.
reason: Baseline by arm required to judge balance.

name: Attrition and noncompliance reported by arm
definition: Attrition/noncompliance is reported only overall or not at all, with no test of differential attrition.
reason: Attrition by arm required.

name: Prespecified primary outcome identified and fully defined
definition: The prespecified primary outcome/analysis is not identified, defined (how/when measured), or changes are undisclosed.
divergence: jaanch applies it from paper text only (registration not fetched); full check needs the registration.
reason: Primary outcome identified and changes disclosed.

name: Deviations from plan and post hoc additions disclosed
definition: Analyses diverge from the pre-analysis plan, or were added after seeing results, without disclosure and reason.
divergence: design-analysis lists PAP elements to compare; assess adds 'preserve negative findings'; audit-analysis adds both adjusted and unadjusted estimates with pre-specified one labeled. jaanch has it only for experiments (prereg_primary_outcome).
reason: Deviations from plan disclosed.

name: Retrospective plan not claimed as prospectively blinded
definition: The paper claims a plan was blinded to outcomes when the record (e.g. a git tag) cannot establish it.
reason: Blinding claim contradicted by version record.

name: Collected measures and computed analyses all reported
definition: Measures collected or analyses computed (in code) are absent from the paper with no 'what we do not report' disclosure.
divergence: I4R diffs code against paper; write-empirical-paper only checks a README disclosure section exists; APA asks to define all measures incl. unreported ones (paper_text only).
reason: Measures in code absent from paper.

name: Sample-size/power analysis reported with all inputs
definition: No power analysis is reported, it is post hoc, or it omits test, N, alpha, target power or effect size.
divergence: No tool of ours. metacheck splits presence (regex) from completeness (LLM on 'power' paragraphs).
validation: metacheck presence: 128 papers, 246 statements, PPV 90.6% (203 TP / 21 FP / 22 FN).
reason: Power analysis with inputs required.

name: Sex of subjects reported and considered
definition: The sex of human or animal subjects is not reported or analyzed.
reason: Sex not reported limits generalization across sexes.

name: Amount and handling of missing data reported
definition: Missing data on key variables is never mentioned, or a handling method is named without how much data it affects.
reason: Missing data amount and handling required.

name: Test statistics sufficient to reconstruct each test
definition: Inferential tests lack exact p, df/MS or other minimal statistics, effect sizes or CIs.
divergence: Umbrella of the three metacheck regex checks below.
reason: Minimal statistics to reconstruct tests required.

name: Effect sizes accompany t and F tests
definition: A t- or F-test in running text has no accompanying effect size.
validation: 161 papers, 1,469 tests; PPV 96%.
reason: Effect sizes with t/F tests required.

name: Exact p-values instead of inequalities or n.s.
definition: p-values above .001 are reported as inequalities (p < .05) or 'n.s.'.
validation: 226 papers, 5,019 p-values; precision 93%, recall 89%.
reason: Exact p-values required.

name: No p-value reported as exactly zero
definition: A p-value is printed as p = .000 instead of p < .001.
reason: p = .000 misreports value.

name: SEM/CFA estimator and fit indices reported
definition: A CFA/SEM does not name its estimator, or describes fit as 'good' without chi-square/df and CFI/RMSEA/SRMR.
reason: CFA/SEM estimator and fit needed for measurement model.

name: IV specification fully named
definition: The IV model does not name outcome, endogenous regressors, excluded instruments, controls, sample, clustering or why treatment is endogenous.
reason: IV specification needed to judge identification.

name: IV first stage and reduced form shown
definition: An IV paper shows no first stage or reduced form with uncertainty and partial R-squared.
reason: First stage and reduced form required.

name: DiD treatment timing and cohort sizes shown
definition: A staggered DiD does not show treatment timing, cohort sizes or the never/not-yet-treated comparison.
reason: DiD timing and cohorts required.

name: ML compute, risks and venue checklist disclosed
definition: An ML paper omits compute, risk discussion or experimental details required by the venue (NeurIPS) checklist.
divergence: No tool of ours.
validation: ReviewerGPT GPT-4: 86.6% accuracy on 119 checklist question-paper pairs; PaperAudit Qwen3-14B SFT+RL 55.8% F1 over all categories.
reason: ML venue checklist items required.

name: Element a referee expects for this design absent
definition: An analysis, test, disclosure or guideline item expected for the paper's design is absent and a main claim depends on it.
divergence: jaanch flags only if a main claim depends on it and excludes Pass-1 items; coarse asks what a top venue expects (no dependency gate); StatReviewer maps text to the named reporting guideline (CONSORT/STROBE) deterministically.
validation: Dawes: all 7 errors no system caught are omissions (best single system 71/100). AMICUS: 7.4% of flags flip on recoding identical text; checklists catch 37% of method flags naive review misses.
reason: Design-expected element absent.

name: Main quantities computed for a concrete model
definition: A theory/econometrics paper never computes its main quantities for one fully specified standard model.
divergence: No tool of ours.
reason: Main quantities never computed for concrete model.

name: Authors identify the paper's own weaknesses
definition: The paper does not acknowledge its main weaknesses or limitations.
divergence: No tool of ours.
reason: Limitations not acknowledged.

name: Estimand of each claim statable in one sentence
definition: For a central claim, unit, population, treatment, outcome, contrast, weighting or time window cannot be recovered.
divergence: Element lists differ: assess adds decision maker and behavioral stage; design-analysis adds aggregation/weighting and time window; audit-analysis records only outcome/unit/comparison/population; EPS applies it to a problem statement (metric, unit, population, magnitude, onset), not a paper.
reason: Estimand of each claim stated.

name: Unit and denominator of each number named
definition: A headline number or table does not say whether it counts people, visits, images, clusters, etc., or its denominator.
divergence: audit-analysis scopes to headline numbers; write-empirical-paper to every quantity; visualize-evidence to table headers/notes.
reason: Unit and denominator of each number named.

name: Effects translated to substantive units and benchmarks
definition: An effect is reported only as a coefficient, star or SD units, without raw-unit magnitude, benchmark or what the interval excludes.
divergence: audit-analysis requires both raw and standardized; design-analysis adds 'what magnitudes the interval excludes'; assess adds empirical benchmarks.
reason: Magnitude in substantive units needed to judge importance.

name: Each result paragraph gives estimate and uncertainty
definition: A result is stated in prose without the estimate, its uncertainty and scope condition.
reason: Estimate and uncertainty per result.

name: Percent changes and ratios name base and direction
definition: A percentage change or ratio does not name its base and direction (45% higher vs 45% lost; women per 1,000 men).
reason: Percent change base and direction named.

name: Percentage-point differences not labeled as percent
definition: A difference between percentages is reported as percent instead of percentage points (or levels/proportions mislabeled).
divergence: visualize-evidence table_unit_labels bundles pp, proportion scale and ratio base; write-empirical-paper splits them into three rules. Regex-able; no script ships.
reason: Percentage points mislabeled as percent.

name: 'Proportion' used only for 0-1 values
definition: A value called a proportion is not on a 0-to-1 scale.
reason: 'Proportion' label on non-0-1 value.

name: Comparison baseline type and denominator named
definition: A percentage is computed against an unnamed or wrong baseline (pooled vs conditional vs model-adjusted).
reason: Percentage baseline unnamed or wrong.

name: Mean-of-ratios vs ratio-of-means choice stated
definition: The paper does not say which ratio estimand it uses, or treats the two as robustness variants.
reason: Ratio estimand choice stated.

name: Weighted and unweighted estimates labeled as different questions
definition: Weighted and unweighted estimates are presented as a robustness pair rather than labeled by estimand.
reason: Weighted and unweighted are different estimands.

name: Identification bounds and sampling CIs reported separately
definition: Identification bounds and sampling confidence intervals are merged into one interval.
reason: Identification and sampling uncertainty separate.

name: Winsorizing/trimming disclosed and trimmed results shown both ways
definition: A published statistic inherits undisclosed winsorizing/trimming, or trimmed results are shown without untrimmed.
reason: Winsorizing disclosed and shown both ways.

name: Data collection choices attributed to actual producer
definition: Collection choices are attributed to the authors when another producer made them, or a questionnaire item is taken as proof data were released.
reason: Collection choices attributed to actual producer.

name: Hand-typed numbers marked with producing script
definition: A number in the manuscript source is a literal not generated by code and carries no comment naming its source.
divergence: Needs LaTeX source; scriptable but no script ships.
reason: Hand-typed numbers marked with source.

name: Model comparison reports flip matrix, not aggregate only
definition: A classifier/model change reports only the aggregate metric change, hiding right-to-wrong flips.
reason: Aggregate metric hides right-to-wrong flips.

name: Fix does not materially raise runtime or spend
