definition: A proposed fix raises runtime, latency or spend materially without saying so.
divergence: Operational; marginal for paper audits.
reason: Agent's fix cost; engineering, not paper.

name: Exhibit readable alone: caption states comparison, universe, marks
definition: A table/figure cannot be read without the text: caption omits what is compared, analytic universe, mark meanings, uncertainty method, exclusions or benchmark.
divergence: visualize-evidence gives an ordered element list and records estimand/denominator/grouping; jaanch only flags 'cannot be read without hunting', capped at 15 passages, severity minor.
reason: Caption must stand alone.

name: Each exhibit answers one stated comparison
definition: An exhibit has no identifiable comparison, or figures/tables do not convey the paper's critical points.
reason: Exhibit has a stated comparison.

name: Exhibit documents data source and analytic choices
definition: An exhibit has no source note or documentation of selection/analytic choices.
reason: Exhibit documents source and analytic choices.

name: Axis and column labels carry units and rescaling
definition: An axis or column has no unit, or a rescaling ('(00s)') is not visible where the number is read.
divergence: audit-analysis adds 'a share column must not hold a count'.
reason: Axis units labeled.

name: Interval level, type, method and clustering stated
definition: An error bar or interval does not name its level, type, construction method or clustering unit.
reason: Interval level and construction stated.

name: Bayesian intervals labeled credible with mass and construction
definition: A Bayesian interval is called a confidence interval or lacks probability mass/construction.
reason: Bayesian intervals labeled credible.

name: Wide intervals not clipped or hidden
definition: An interval is truncated or uncertainty removed for layout reasons.
reason: Clipped intervals hide uncertainty.

name: Reference lines mark a real, labeled benchmark
definition: A reference line is arbitrary or unlabeled.
reason: Reference lines labeled.

name: Two-three significant digits, constant within column
definition: Numbers show false precision or mixed precision within a row/column.
divergence: Partly scriptable; no script ships.
reason: Significant digits convention.

name: No raw 'nan'; dashes explained in note
definition: A table prints 'nan' or an unexplained dash for an unavailable estimate.
divergence: Trivially grep-able; no script ships.
reason: No raw 'nan'.

name: No table shipped with header but no estimates
definition: An output table has a header but its rows/estimates are absent.
reason: Table shipped without estimates.

name: Model results shown on interpretable scale
definition: Model results are shown as raw link-scale coefficients where predictions/contrasts are needed (e.g. logit interactions).
reason: Link-scale coefficients need interpretable scale.

name: Graphic keeps raw-data or model context
definition: A summary graphic strips the raw-data/model context that would reveal the claim's weakness.
reason: Graphic strips context revealing weakness.

name: Map caption distinguishes what each mark represents
definition: A map caption does not distinguish sampled units, routes, observation points and boundaries.
reason: Map caption distinguishes mark types.

name: No bar charts for continuous data
definition: A bar graph summarizes continuous data, hiding its distribution.
divergence: No tool of ours.
validation: Barzooka precision 0.95 / recall 0.91 internal; 0.94 / 0.92 external (Riedel 2022).
reason: No bar charts for continuous data.

name: Quantitative comparisons use position, not area/angle
definition: A pie, bubble or area encoding is used for a precise quantitative comparison.
divergence: Barzooka only detects pie charts (script); visualize-evidence judges any area/angle/volume encoding (model).
validation: Barzooka pie chart precision 0.97 / recall 0.92.
reason: Position encoding preferred.

name: Chart form matches the comparison task
definition: The chart form hides the comparison (e.g. bars for estimates instead of dot-and-interval; graph where a table is needed).
reason: Chart form fits task.

name: Lines only connect ordered, continuous x values
definition: A line connects unordered categories or implies a trajectory that does not exist.
reason: Lines need ordered x.

name: Map used only when geography is the question
definition: A map is used where a ranked dot-and-interval display would answer the question better.
reason: Map only when geography matters.

name: Groups labeled directly, not via arbitrary legend
definition: Group identity is encoded by arbitrary colors/shapes decoded through a legend.
reason: Direct labels over legends.

name: Rows ordered by value or substantive order
definition: Rows/categories are ordered alphabetically or by arbitrary ID.
reason: Meaningful row order.

name: Overplotting handled so multiplicity visible
definition: A scatter hides most observations through overplotting.
reason: Overplotting handled.

name: Palette type matches data type
definition: A diverging palette is used without a meaningful midpoint, or palette type mismatches the data.
reason: Palette matches data type.

name: Legible in grayscale and color-vision deficiency
definition: A distinction is carried only by hue.
reason: Legible without hue.

name: Web exhibits meet WCAG contrast ratios
definition: A foreground/background pair falls below 4.5:1 (text), 3:1 (large text / graphical objects).
divergence: Deterministic; no script ships.
reason: WCAG contrast thresholds.

name: Axis labels and annotations not faint gray
definition: Axis labels, denominators or uncertainty annotations are rendered in low-contrast text.
reason: Essential text not faint.

name: Each table has one job
definition: A table mixes unrelated purposes without labeled blocks.
reason: Each table one job.

name: Booktabs rules, no vertical lines, decimal alignment
definition: A table uses vertical rules or misaligned numbers.
divergence: House style.
reason: Booktabs convention.

name: Exported figures embed fonts with no substitution
definition: An exported PDF/SVG has substituted fonts, missing glyphs, kerning or clipping problems.
divergence: pdffonts could automate; no script ships.
reason: Fonts embedded.

name: Every compiled page inspected at delivery size
definition: A compiled page has a clipped, overlapping or unreadable element.
reason: Every page inspected rendered.

name: Author-year citation forms render correctly
definition: Textual or parenthetical citations render as numeric or malformed in the compiled PDF.
divergence: House style.
reason: Citation forms render.

name: Terms and symbols defined before use
definition: A term, symbol or abbreviation is used before definition, or defined differently in two places.
divergence: Second half overlaps consistency definitions/notation check.
reason: Terms defined before use.

name: Referents ('this', 'the effect') resolvable
definition: A reader cannot tell what 'this', 'the effect' or 'the model' refers to.
reason: Referents resolvable.

name: Main result easy to find and stated directly
definition: A main result is hard to find or stated only indirectly.
reason: Main result easy to find.

name: Key passages follow premise-to-conclusion order
definition: A key passage buries its logic in long qualification chains or states the conclusion before premises.
reason: Logic order hard to follow.

name: Language, notation and argument communicate effectively
definition: Language, notation, arguments or visualizations impede understanding (meaning-level, not cosmetic).
divergence: Stanford gives a score, not findings; ScholScan requires evidence localization. Our jaanch splits this into the four specific writing checks above.
validation: Stanford: Spearman AI-human 0.42 vs human-human 0.41 (overall score, not clarity alone).
reason: General clarity.

name: Research question and abstract framed for impact
definition: The research question, pitch or abstract could be reframed to state contribution more clearly.
divergence: No tool of ours.
validation: ReviewerGPT GPT-4: 4/10 better-abstract picks correct (near chance).
reason: Framing of contribution.

name: No unqualified superlatives or exaggerated novelty
definition: The paper uses unqualified superlatives or claims novelty/dominance it does not support.
divergence: Overlaps reasoning-category overclaiming checks (not in this slice).
reason: Superlatives and novelty overclaimed.

name: Typos and numbering errors
definition: The text has typos or misnumbered sections, equations, tables or figures.
divergence: jaanch writing explicitly excludes style/grammar unless meaning changes.
validation: ~10% wrong-error rate in secondary press only: unverified.
reason: Typos and numbering.

name: No placeholder or TODO text left
definition: The draft contains '??', [TODO] or conditional placeholder phrasing.
divergence: Regex-able ('??' is also LaTeX's unresolved-ref marker); coarse uses an LLM.
reason: Placeholder text left.

name: Public audit output avoids adversarial tone
definition: A public replication output uses adversarial headings, verdicts or motive speculation.
divergence: Checks our own output, not the audited paper.
reason: Tone of public audit output.

name: Public summary separates verified errors from limits
definition: A public summary blurs verified errors with measurement limits, assumptions or untested explanations.
divergence: Checks our own output; corrigendum skill draws the same distinction (not rowed here).
reason: Audit summary separates errors from limits.

name: Manipulation moved the intended construct
definition: An experiment whose effect is attributed to a changed belief, emotion or salience shows evidence the treatment changed it, not only that it was delivered.
reason: Shadish, Cook and Campbell (2002) ch. 3: construct validity of the cause

name: DiD estimate presented as effect on the treated
definition: A difference-in-differences estimate is the average effect on treated units; extending it to untreated units or a wider rollout needs its own argument.
reason: Roth, Sant'Anna, Bilinski and Poe (2023)
